A minimum QQI Level 5 qualification in social care or equivalent qualification
Minimum 2-years’ experience in intellectual disabilities (related field experience considered)
Managing your time effectively, working autonomously and demonstrating initiative.
Ability to manage behaviours that may challenge
A satisfactory level of IT proficiency for use of online/assistive technology
Commitment to best practice guidelines, to regulations, and to L’Arche policy, especially regarding safeguarding, upholding confidentiality, and accountability
Full clean driving licence
The post is subject to Garda vetting
Special Circumstances:
Some degree of flexible working, in order to meet the needs of the person you support
Salary scale:
HSE Health Care Assistant 30,216-45,976 Euros per annum, pro rata
Please refer to Job Description for further details of the role. Queries about the post should be directed to the Day Service Co-Ordinator by phone or email as follows, Tel: 021-431-8880 or Email: meadhbh.furlong@larche.ie. L’Arche Cork is an equal opportunities employer.

Job Description
Job Description – Outreach Day Service Support (part-time – 15 hours)
Overview:
L’Arche Cork is recruiting for the position of Care Assistant to provide an outreach day service to support a 65-year-old woman in her home whilst recuperating from a fall. The distribution of the 15 hours throughout the week is subject to discussion. The role will require supporting the person to sometimes physically attend L’Arche day service. This work will be conducted in adherence to the highest standard of care and support, in accordance with the ethos of the L’Arche Community and with the relevant national policies, standards, and legislation, specifically New Directions Interim Standards for Adult Disability Services, and the National Framework for Person Centred Planning in Services for Persons with a Disability.
Location:
At a private family residence in the general area of Cobh, County Cork and at L’Arche Togher, as required
Reporting to:
Day Service Co-Ordinator, L’Arche Cork/Day Service Team Lead
Main purpose:
The role of any frontline worker in L’Arche is to support and enable adults with intellectual disability (ID) to improve their quality of life, and to achieve equality and independence through meeting their social support needs. This specific role involves providing an outreach day service for a 65-year-old woman in her own home due to her recently-reduced capacity to attend L’Arche’s day service. The focus of the support will be to maintain social connectedness for this woman through conversation, music, zoom calls with L’Arche staff, and board or card games. The use of online/assistive technology would greatly improve quality of life for this woman and as such some IT proficiency is essential. The role will involve some personal care whilst immobile (in addition to that provided by Home Help three times a day). As the person’s condition is expected to improve, she may return to the day service in a much-reduced capacity. If this improvement unfolds, the Outreach Day Service Support/Care Assistant would be expected to convey the person to and from L’Arche.
Position Summary:
The Outreach Day Service Support/Care Assistant will play an advocacy role in helping to meet the social support needs of this person, with a focus on wellbeing and accessibility.
Duties and responsibilities:
Supporting the person in the following areas:
Personal care- Toileting as required (Note that Home Help attends three times day to assist in this regard and to wash and dress the person)
Medical needs-Monitor the well-being of the person, in close liaison with the guardian, accompanying the person to medical appointments, and administering medication, as required. Keep records of all medical events.
Health promotion-Encourage good health habits including appropriate exercise (in consultation with any other professionals involved in the person’s care such as Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist etc.), diet, and relaxation techniques.
Spirituality – To support the person’s spiritual needs, such as, for example, engagement in religious service of their choosing, Mindfulness practice etc.
Activities appropriate to the individual- Encouraging and supporting participation in activities or pastimes appropriate to the person’s level of ability, interest areas, and in accordance with their expressed preferences.
Active citizenship - Encouraging and supporting the person to engage with community groups with similar interests or hobbies, including sometimes transport. This would include visits to L’Arche in Togher. Activities for this particular person might include taking car trips to places of interest, online or chair yoga/qi gong (run at L’Arche)
Safeguarding - Ensuring the safety and wellbeing, both of yourself and the person you support, with respect for risk assessments, incident reports and adherence to best practice guidelines and organisational policy.
Driving- Driving the person you support to appointments, to L’Arche community events, or on trips out locally.
Quality:
Aligning with New Directions standards, to ensure that the service you provide to the person/people you support is safe, responsive to individual needs, and high quality
To be cognisant of continuous professional development in terms of self-recognised or service-identified training needs
To be cognisant of continuous service improvement, consistently documenting and reviewing services, in consultation with the person/people availing of those services, to ensure that they are meeting the needs of those individuals and promoting positive outcomes
To obtain feedback from the person/people you support, and their circles of support, with regard to service development, improvement, and change
To comply with and contribute to day service monitoring systems
Communication and Reporting:
Forging a positive and trusting relationship with the person you support and the person’s guardian
To report directly to the Day Service Co-Ordinator/Dy Service Team Lead
Liaison with Day Support Staff as required (with regard to social events of interest to the person you support, planned community events, external facilitator activities etc.)
To attend regular support and supervision sessions with the Day Service Co-Ordinator - to ensure adequate support is available to you and to the person you support, and to identify training needs
To facilitate person centred planning (PCP) meetings and reviews for the person you support
To attend other meetings relating to the person you support, when necessary, such as multi-disciplinary case conferences, or L’Arche Community r

jobs.title: Part Time Commercial Co-Founder – Equity-Based Opportunity

Help build the next big Irish parenting platform. Share in the journey and the value you help create.
Have you got the experience, entrepreneurial mindset and ambition to help grow an exciting early-stage business?
We're looking to connect with an experienced, commercially minded individual who would like to play a key role in developing and growing
Lullagram
http://lullagram.ie/ an Irish parenting technology platform with ambitions to become Ireland's leading destination for parents and families.
About Lullagram
Lullagram is building an integrated platform designed to support families through every stage of their parenting journey, from fertility and pregnancy through to newborn care, childcare, education and family life.
Our vision is to bring together parents, professionals, services and resources in one trusted digital ecosystem.
We're developing opportunities across:
Parenting apps and digital memberships.
A national directory and marketplace of parenting professionals.
Childcare and childminder discovery.
Fertility, pregnancy and postnatal support.
Online programmes, classes and expert services.
Corporate parental support and employer partnerships.
Strategic partnerships across family services and financial wellbeing.
The opportunity
We're looking for someone who can work alongside the founder to help turn this vision into a commercially successful and scalable business.
This is an opportunity to get involved at an early stage, influence the direction of the company and help build something with genuine potential.
Areas of responsibility would include:
Developing and executing the commercial growth strategy.
Identifying and securing strategic partnerships.
Building relationships with childcare, parenting and healthcare professionals.
Developing employer and corporate partnerships.
Identifying revenue opportunities and commercial models.
Helping grow the platform and establish its position in the Irish market.
Bringing fresh ideas, experience and entrepreneurial thinking to the business.
Who we're looking for
We're particularly interested in someone who:
Has experience in business development, commercial strategy, sales, partnerships or entrepreneurship.
Has a track record of building relationships and creating business opportunities.
Is commercially minded, proactive and comfortable working independently.
Understands what it takes to grow an early-stage business.
Has an entrepreneurial mindset and wants to be involved in building something rather than simply taking on another job.
Experience in technology, digital platforms, healthcare, childcare, family services or startups would be a distinct advantage.
You may currently be working in a senior commercial role, running your own business or consulting and looking for an exciting opportunity to become involved in another venture.
The arrangement.Please read

We're therefore exploring a part-time, equity-based commercial partnership or co-founder arrangement with the right individual.

We're open to speaking with potential strategic investors who may also bring relevant business experience, industry knowledge or valuable connections.
Investment and operational involvement would be considered as separate opportunities.
Interested?
If this sounds like something you'd be interested in exploring, we'd love to hear from you.
Please get in touch with a brief introduction outlining:
Your professional background and experience.
What you could potentially bring to Lullagram.
Why the opportunity interests you.
Whether you're interested in a commercial partnership, co-founder opportunity or investment.
We're not just looking for someone to fill a position. We're looking for the right person to help build something meaningful.
hello@lullagram.ie

LULLAGRAM | Supporting families through every stage of the journey.

jobs.title: Graduate Bridge & Civil Structures
jobs.desc:
See it differently
You see the world through a unique lens and that’s exactly what we need. We embrace how you see things differently – it’s essential for creating a sustainable future.
Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates and students who help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities.
The Opportunity
At Arup, our Bridge & Civil Structures Engineers design and deliver some of the world's most complex and iconic infrastructure projects. From bridges, highways and rail networks to major transportation and civic infrastructure, we bring together technical excellence, innovation and sustainable design to create solutions that make a positive impact.
As a Graduate Bridge & Civil Structures Engineer, you'll work alongside experienced engineers on challenging projects while developing the technical, digital and professional skills needed to build a rewarding engineering career.
As a Graduate Bridge & Civil Structures Engineer at Arup, you will (but not limited to):
Support the analysis and design of bridges, retaining structures and civil engineering infrastructure.
Assist in the preparation of engineering calculations, technical reports, specifications and design documentation.
Develop structural models and undertake engineering assessments using industry-standard software.
Contribute to the design of sustainable, resilient and efficient infrastructure solutions.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams including highways, rail, geotechnical, environmental and digital engineering specialists.
Support the production and coordination of drawings and BIM deliverables.
Participate in site visits, inspections, surveys and construction support activities.
Help deliver projects through all stages of the design lifecycle, from concept development to detailed design and construction.
Apply engineering principles to solve complex structural challenges and improve project outcomes.
Is this role right for you?
For this opportunity, we are seeking the following qualifications, skills and attributes:
An undergraduate or bachelor's degree (minimum NFQ Level 8 or equivalent) in one of the following disciplines:
Civil Engineering
Structural Engineering
Civil & Structural Engineering
Infrastructure Engineering
Engineering with Structural Design
Architectural Engineering (with a structural focus)
A related engineering discipline accredited by Engineers Ireland or an equivalent professional institution
Applicants studying towards a Master's degree are strongly encouraged to apply
Desired Skills & Knowledge, What We Are Looking For
A keen interest in bridge engineering and civil structures.
Understanding structural analysis and design principles.
Knowledge of steel, reinforced concrete, prestressed concrete and composite structures.
Familiarity with engineering software such as AutoCAD, Revit, Civil 3D, Tekla Structures, SOFiSTiK, MIDAS, LUSAS, Robot Structural Analysis or similar.
An interest in digital engineering, BIM and innovative design technologies.
Knowledge of sustainable design principles and modern construction methods.
Desired Personal Attributes, What We Are Looking For
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Attention to detail and commitment to technical excellence.
A collaborative approach and ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
Curiosity, initiative and a passion for engineering.
Enthusiasm for delivering infrastructure that improves communities and supports a sustainable future.
To Be Considered For a Graduate Opportunity, Your Application Must Include a Copy Of Your Academic Transcript And Meet The Following Criteria
No more than 12 months of full-time experience in a comparable role
Recently graduated, or on track to graduate, from your most recent degree, related to your role of choice, before employment starts.
Closing date:
12 November 2026
Please note, in the event of high applicant volume, this role may be closed ahead of the advertised closing date. We advise that you apply early.
Eligibility
We're able to consider candidates who require an employment permit to work in Ireland, where the role and offered salary meet the Irish Government's eligibility criteria (for example, under the Critical Skills or General Employment Permit schemes). All Employment Permits are granted at the discretion of the Deciding Officer with offers contingent to obtaining the correct immigration to work and reside in Ireland.
What we offer you
At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.
Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.
We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling permanent members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
We take an approach to flexible working that supports the diversity and wellbeing of our graduates.
Regional Addition
For our permanent members we offer private medical insurance allowances, life assurance and income protection cover.
Different people, shared values
Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas - this drives our excellence.
Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup . We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas.
We are committed to providing an inclusive recruitment process. Candidates may inform us of any disability, learning difference, or other circumstance that may require reasonable adjustments for interviews or assessments. Any information provided will be used only to make appropriate arrangements and will not be considered in any other aspect of your application or selection process.

As a Tendering Project Engineer in EPS, you will play a crucial role in the preparation and submission of competitive bids for various water and wastewater projects. Your expertise will be essential in ensuring that our proposals meet the technical, commercial and regulatory requirements while also aligning with our company's strategic objectives. This position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to the development of sustainable water solutions and to work on innovative projects that make a positive impact on communities and the environment. A highly varied, challenging role providing invaluable exposure to the right candidate. Projects are primarily focused on Process/Mechanical/Electrical/ICA requirements with minor civil works included. Reviewing Tender documents, interpreting specifications and understanding customers needs. Developing designs and project build bill of materials to ensure accurate and value for money solutions can be provided. Developing P & Ids and layout Tender Drawings where required. Reviewing commercial terms and conditions. Preparation of Technical Tender submissions and supporting Health & Safety and Quality documentation. Where required, ensuring projects are delivered without any compromise on safety and quality, co-ordinating safety and liaising with our HSQE department. Ensuring submissions meet client specifications and project scopes. Supporting the design team in delivering innovative solutions and using modern technologies. Supporting project delivering team with design and procurement to achieve a successful project delivery. Creating the project programme and ensuring that all required project interfaces are allowed for, from design to final site commissioning and handover. Get involved in project delivery where required including liaising and co-ordinating all works with the client and relevant stakeholders. Writing engineering reports, method statements and commissioning schedules. Key Competencies and Skills: Proficiency in PC skills. Excellent inter-personal and communication skills. Strong engineering analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong commercial understanding of contracting deliverables. Strong collaborative skills with an ability to work effectively in a team environment. Have a willingness to learn and be challenged in the water and wastewater Industry. Have proven experience in a similar design & engineering role in a Mechanical & Electrical environment. Experience in implementing opportunities and initiatives in a time restricted schedule. Organise and plan technical meetings with clients and Consulting Engineers. Develop specific goals and plans to prioritise, organise and accomplish stated deadlines. Project management / Site management / M&E Installation, Personnel Management and any Water &/or Wastewater industry experience will be an advantage. Qualifications: Third level Mechanical, Civil or Electrical Engineering degree/diploma Similar relevant third level qualification and experience will be considered Full EU/ Irish driving licence Compensation Package: Competitive salary and benefits package Opportunities for professional development and career growth CPD accredited employer A collaborative and supportive work environment Laptop or desktop and work mobile phone provided Flexible working options, dependent on location and role requirements See company website for more information on the benefits of working in EPS Group We welcome speculative applications from individuals of all levels. Equal Opportunity Statement - EPS Group is an equal opportunities employer. jobs.desc:
ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.
At AMD, we believe technology can change lives for the better. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we’re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don’t shy away from humanity’s challenges but are determined to help solve them.
AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward.
As an AMD intern, you’ll be placed at the epicenter of the AI ecosystem, working alongside experts and industry pioneers. You’ll do important work, learn new skills, expand your network, and gain real-world experience on projects that impact millions of end-users worldwide. Whether you’re an undergrad or a PhD student, your contributions matter—and your experience here will be a launchpad for what comes next.
An exciting internship opportunity to make an immediate contribution to AMD's next generation of technology innovations awaits you! We have a multifaceted, high-energy work environment, filled with a diverse group of employees, and we provide outstanding opportunities for developing your career. During your internship, you will have the opportunity to collaborate with AMD leaders, receive one-on-one mentorship, attend amazing networking events, and much more. Being part of AMD means receiving hands-on experience that will give you a competitive edge. Together We Advance your career!
Job Details
Location: Cork or Dublin, Ireland
Onsite: This role requires the student to work full time onsite throughout the duration of the intern term
Duration: Students must be available to start on January 15th (Cork or Dublin) or June 1st (Cork-only)for a 6-month internship
About The Team
The AMD SerDes team in Ireland develops high-speed SerDes solutions operating at 200+ Gb/s using advanced CMOS FinFET technologies. The team has extensive expertise in the design of analog and mixed-signal circuits for the high-speed transmission, reception, clocking, and recovery of data over wired links. The successful candidate will join a world-class engineering team developing advanced SerDes solutions that enable high-performance connectivity across AMD CPU, GPU, and FPGA products.
The Analog Mixed-Signal (AMS) team designs high-performance analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits, including ADCs, DACs, voltage and current references, clocking circuits, regulators, high-speed interfaces, and SerDes-related analog building blocks. As part of AMD's IC design team, you will work alongside experienced analog and mixed-signal designers and gain hands-on exposure to the complete IC design flow, from circuit specifications and architecture through transistor-level design, simulation, layout, verification, and post-layout analysis.
The internship is designed to provide practical experience in analog and mixed-signal IC design using industry-leading design tools, advanced CMOS technologies, and professional design methodologies.
What You Will Be Doing
As an Analog & Mixed-Signal Design Intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers and gain hands-on experience designing advanced integrated circuits, including high-speed SerDes.
Learn how system requirements are translated into analog and mixed-signal circuit designs.
Support the design, simulation and optimization of transistor-level circuits.
Work with analog building blocks such as amplifiers, bias circuits, voltage/current references, data converters, clocking circuits and high-speed interfaces.
Run simulations across different operating conditions and analyse key performance metrics such as gain, bandwidth, noise, power, jitter and stability.
Gain exposure to custom IC layout, including matching, placement, routing and parasitic effects.
Evaluate designs through pre-layout and post-layout simulation and verification.
Participate in design reviews and share your findings with experienced engineers.
Gain hands-on experience with industry-standard IC design and simulation tools.
Who We Are Looking For
You are currently enrolled in university in a program majoring in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Microelectronics, Integrated Circuit Design, or a related discipline, and have an interest in analog and mixed-signal IC design.
If you have experience with any of the following technical skills (or related areas) and are enthusiastic about this role, we strongly encourage you to apply -
Electronic circuit fundamentals, including MOS transistors and transistor-level circuit analysis.
Analog concepts such as biasing, differential amplifiers, feedback, frequency response, stability, noise and device matching.
Familiarity with analog/mixed-signal circuits such as ADCs, DACs, PLLs, regulators, references or high-speed interfaces.
Exposure to SPICE-based circuit simulation or analog IC design environments.
Familiarity with tools such as Cadence Virtuoso, Spectre, Synopsys Custom Compiler or HSPICE is an advantage, but not required.
Basic knowledge of custom IC layout or physical design.
Experience with Python, MATLAB, Tcl, Perl, or similar tools for data analysis or automation.
Analytical, problem-solving and communication skills.
Curiosity, initiative and an interest in developing your skills in analog/mixed-signal IC design, high-speed circuits and leading-edge CMOS technologies.
Note:
By submitting your application, you are indicating your interest in AMD intern positions. We are recruiting for multiple positions, and if your experience aligns with any of our intern opportunities, a recruiter will contact you.

At L'Occitane en Provence, your passion for beauty and sustainability creates meaningful impact. Join us to craft authentic beauty experiences, care for the planet, and connect with guests in a beautiful environment where your growth and development are truly nurtured.

Contribution Pension Scheme

Mercedes-Benz Cork, a principal dealer for Mercedes-Benz in Ireland and Cork's exclusive Mercedes-Benz dealership, currently wish to recruit a full-time Valetor to join our team in our modern-indoor valeting department at our three-story dealership facility located in Eastgate Business Park, Little Island, Co. Cork.
We are a sister company of MDL (Motor Distributors Limited) which are the importers for Mercedes-Benz in Ireland. Our dealership, located in East Gate Business Park, Little Island, County Cork, operates a Sales, Service, Repair and Parts facility dedicated to Mercedes-Benz.
At Mercedes-Benz Cork, we take pride in our commitment to our employees, focusing on providing a positive working environment, while also offering excellent training and development opportunities. We provide a long-standing career rather than just a job, with continuous development initiatives, opportunities for progression, and competitive remuneration packages, all contributing to the loyalty of our team.
Key duties & Responsibilities;
Vehicle - Cleaning/Cleansing/Decontamination.
Vehicle hand washing using twin grit guard bucket system to prevent any stones and sharp-edged particles being carried onto the car via wash mitt.
Removal of tar, road grime, honey dew and bug splatter deposits and other petroleum-based substances by applying body solvent to dissolve particles.
Vehicle hand drying using deep-pile microfibre towels.
Tyres and Exterior plastics and door trims dressing.
Paint Correction to remove light paint imperfections, such as minor swirl marks to increase the gloss factor.
Shampooing carpets if necessary and dried using a wet suction vacuum cleaner. All leather surfaces are cleansed and protected. Air vents, button surrounds and fascia are cleaned using specialised brushes.
Vacuuming carpets, Windows are cleaned on the inside.
Interior trim and surfaces are all cleaned using aerospace-grade products.
Application of Mercedes-Benz approved interior and exterior protection products.
Assist in the responsibility for the condition of all new and used cars being delivered to our customers, inspecting vehicles with sales and service personal prior to customer handover.
Ensure that the condition of our used car display area is up to an auditable standard by a third party.
Keep work areas clean and tidy, organised and safe from hazards in accordance with health and safety guidelines.
The successful candidate will ideally:
Have previous valeting experience.

jobs.title: Software Engineer 3

The Kubernetes teams make running MongoDB in and from Kubernetes so frictionless that it is the default database choice for cloud-native applications. Our operators let developers and platform teams provision, scale and operate MongoDB through Kubernetes-native APIs, in their own clusters or in MongoDB Atlas.
You will join the Kubernetes Capabilities squad. Our sister squad builds the shared platform layer of the MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes; we build the capabilities on top of it that users actually adopt. That means bringing MongoDB features such as Search and Vector Search to Kubernetes, extending what our users can deploy and manage declaratively, and owning the Atlas Kubernetes Operator. Our work starts with a user problem and ends with a Kubernetes API that solves it.
In practice, we build a platform for other engineers. Our users are developers and platform teams who expect self-service, sensible defaults and APIs that behave predictably. If you have built an internal developer platform, a Kubernetes controller, or any system whose customers are other engineers, you will recognise the problems we work on.
No prior experience with MongoDB is required. You will meet most of the team during interviews, and we pride ourselves on being an inclusive, collaborative group that Builds Together. Our core engineering values are Context, Predictability, Transparency, Focus and Craftsmanship.
This role can be based in our Dublin office, Cork office or remotely within Ireland.
The role
We are looking for a Software Engineer to join the Kubernetes Capabilities squad and help decide which MongoDB capabilities our users get on Kubernetes and how they work. You will own significant capabilities from design to production, make sound technical decisions under ambiguity, and raise the engineering bar of the team through design, review and mentorship.
Experience we value
What matters most is that you have built platforms, not only operated them. We value experience from any of these backgrounds:
Building Kubernetes controllers, operators, CRDs, admission webhooks or other extensions against the Kubernetes API
Building internal developer platforms: self-service provisioning, golden paths, platform APIs, CLIs or developer portals used by other engineering teams
Building developer-facing infrastructure products such as SDKs, managed services, CI/CD systems or cloud provisioning tooling
Responsibilities
Lead the design and delivery of new capabilities in our Kubernetes operators, from technical design through production support
Work with Product and the teams behind MongoDB features to turn them into Kubernetes-native APIs our users can adopt
Write technical designs that weigh trade-offs clearly and bring the team and stakeholders to a decision
Shape our platform APIs with our users in mind: predictable, self-service and safe to operate
Mentor engineers through pairing, code review and design feedback
Partner with our platform squad, Support, Docs and other engineering teams, and help resolve complex customer issues
Improve how the team works, including testing strategy, release quality and developer experience
Requirements
Strong core software engineering skills and several years building production software in a modern language; we mostly use Go
Proven experience building a platform for other engineers, such as Kubernetes controllers and operators, an internal developer platform, or developer-facing infrastructure products
Deep working knowledge of Kubernetes, including its API model, reconciliation and the operational realities of running workloads on it
Experience designing, testing and operating distributed systems in production
A track record of leading projects through ambiguity and delivering them end to end
Strong written communication, including technical design documents
Nice to have
Experience with controller-runtime, kubebuilder or contributing to Kubernetes ecosystem projects
Experience with multi-cluster Kubernetes, networking or service mesh
Experience running stateful workloads or databases on Kubernetes
Experience with a major public cloud provider
What is in it for you
Generous compensation package (top-range salary, equity, comprehensive benefits)
A diverse, highly collaborative team that values shipping fast and clean
Time to learn on the job and grow into new technologies

jobs.title: Software Engineer 3
jobs.desc:
The Kubernetes teams make running MongoDB in and from Kubernetes so frictionless that it is the default database choice for cloud-native applications. Our operators let developers and platform teams provision, scale and operate MongoDB through Kubernetes-native APIs, in their own clusters or in MongoDB Atlas.
You will join the Kubernetes Capabilities squad. Our sister squad builds the shared platform layer of the MongoDB Controllers for Kubernetes; we build the capabilities on top of it that users actually adopt. That means bringing MongoDB features such as Search and Vector Search to Kubernetes, extending what our users can deploy and manage declaratively, and owning the Atlas Kubernetes Operator. Our work starts with a user problem and ends with a Kubernetes API that solves it.
In practice, we build a platform for other engineers. Our users are developers and platform teams who expect self-service, sensible defaults and APIs that behave predictably. If you have built an internal developer platform, a Kubernetes controller, or any system whose customers are other engineers, you will recognise the problems we work on.
No prior experience with MongoDB is required. You will meet most of the team during interviews, and we pride ourselves on being an inclusive, collaborative group that Builds Together. Our core engineering values are Context, Predictability, Transparency, Focus and Craftsmanship.
This role can be based in our Dublin office, Cork office or remotely within Ireland.
The role
We are looking for a Software Engineer to join the Kubernetes Capabilities squad and help decide which MongoDB capabilities our users get on Kubernetes and how they work. You will own significant capabilities from design to production, make sound technical decisions under ambiguity, and raise the engineering bar of the team through design, review and mentorship.
Experience we value
What matters most is that you have built platforms, not only operated them. We value experience from any of these backgrounds:
Building Kubernetes controllers, operators, CRDs, admission webhooks or other extensions against the Kubernetes API
Building internal developer platforms: self-service provisioning, golden paths, platform APIs, CLIs or developer portals used by other engineering teams
Building developer-facing infrastructure products such as SDKs, managed services, CI/CD systems or cloud provisioning tooling
Responsibilities
Lead the design and delivery of new capabilities in our Kubernetes operators, from technical design through production support
Work with Product and the teams behind MongoDB features to turn them into Kubernetes-native APIs our users can adopt
Write technical designs that weigh trade-offs clearly and bring the team and stakeholders to a decision
Shape our platform APIs with our users in mind: predictable, self-service and safe to operate
Mentor engineers through pairing, code review and design feedback
Partner with our platform squad, Support, Docs and other engineering teams, and help resolve complex customer issues
Improve how the team works, including testing strategy, release quality and developer experience
Requirements
Strong core software engineering skills and several years building production software in a modern language; we mostly use Go
Proven experience building a platform for other engineers, such as Kubernetes controllers and operators, an internal developer platform, or developer-facing infrastructure products
Deep working knowledge of Kubernetes, including its API model, reconciliation and the operational realities of running workloads on it
Experience designing, testing and operating distributed systems in production
A track record of leading projects through ambiguity and delivering them end to end
Strong written communication, including technical design documents
Nice to have
Experience with controller-runtime, kubebuilder or contributing to Kubernetes ecosystem projects
Experience with multi-cluster Kubernetes, networking or service mesh
Experience running stateful workloads or databases on Kubernetes
Experience with a major public cloud provider
What is in it for you
Generous compensation package (top-range salary, equity, comprehensive benefits)
A diverse, highly collaborative team that values shipping fast and clean
Time to learn on the job and grow into new technologies
A high level of independence, focused on results rather than the appearance of work
About MongoDB
MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. We have redefined the data platform for the AI era, enabling builders to create, transform, and disrupt industries with software. MongoDB’s unified data platform, the most widely available, globally distributed data platform on the market, helps organizations modernize legacy workloads, embrace innovation, and unleash AI. Our cloud-native platform, MongoDB Atlas, is the only globally distributed, multi-cloud data platform and is available across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.
With offices worldwide and over 67,000 customers, including AI-native startups and approximately 75% of the Fortune 100, relying on MongoDB for their most important applications, we’re powering the next era of software.
Our compass at MongoDB is our Leadership Commitment, guiding how and why we make decisions, show up for each other, and win. It’s what makes us MongoDB.
To drive the personal growth and business impact of our employees, we’re committed to developing a supportive and enriching culture for everyone. From employee affinity groups, to fertility assistance and a generous parental leave policy, we value our employees’ wellbeing and want to support them along every step of their professional and personal journeys. Learn more about what it’s like to work at MongoDB, and help us make an impact on the world!
MongoDB is committed to providing any necessary accommodations for individuals with disabilities within our application and interview process. To request an accommodation due to a disability, please inform your recruiter.
MongoDB is an equal opportunities employer.

jobs.title: Experienced Analog IC Designer
jobs.desc:
Job Description
onsemi is seeking an experienced Analog IC Designer to join its Core Analog IP Development Centre of Excellence in Cork, Ireland. You will develop power, clock, monitoring and reset IP for the Treo platform in BCD65 technology, combining hands-on circuit design with substantial architecture involvement and cross-product-line technical engagement.
This role extends well beyond individual block delivery. You will help shape platform-level analog IP architectures, translate product-line requirements into actionable IP roadmaps for the Core Analog teams, and champion IP reuse across the platform. You will also mentor junior engineers and guide designs from concept and specification through silicon validation and mass production.
Responsibilities
Architecture, Product Engagement and IP Roadmaps
Play a leading technical role in defining architectures for power, clock, monitoring and reset IP in the Treo BCD65 platform.
Engage directly with product-line architects, design teams and stakeholders to understand product needs, operating conditions, integration constraints and future requirements.
Translate these needs into clear IP specifications and prioritised development roadmaps for the Core Analog teams, balancing immediate product commitments with longer-term platform requirements.
Drive architecture trade-offs across performance, power, area, robustness, testability and integration complexity.
Champion reusable IP architectures, configurable features and consistent interfaces that support adoption across multiple products while limiting unnecessary customisation.
Communicate architecture proposals, roadmap priorities and technical decisions clearly through design reviews, presentations and written documentation.
Analog Design and Production Delivery
Design and develop analog IP including bandgap references, low-dropout regulators (LDOs), DC–DC regulators, oscillators, phase-locked loops (PLLs), monitoring circuits and reset functions.
Own block development from specification and circuit architecture through transistor-level design, simulation, layout guidance, verification and silicon characterisation.
Verify performance across process, voltage and temperature corners, including mismatch, noise, stability, start-up behaviour and relevant operating modes.
Work closely with layout engineers to address matching, parasitics, isolation, coupling and device reliability, and ensure post-layout performance meets specifications.
Collaborate with product integration, validation, test and product engineering teams to resolve issues and support successful transfer to mass production.
Create clear design documentation, integration guidance and characterisation reports that enable efficient IP reuse and maintenance.
Technical Leadership, Mentoring and AI Adoption
Mentor junior engineers in analog design fundamentals, architecture evaluation, simulation methodology, design reviews and silicon debug.
Provide technical guidance and constructive design feedback, sharing knowledge and strengthening engineering practices across the Core Analog teams.
Help identify and assess practical opportunities for AI-assisted analog design and layout, including design-space exploration, simulation automation, results analysis, documentation and layout assistance.
Apply sound engineering judgement when evaluating AI-generated outputs, retaining rigorous verification, traceability and protection of confidential design information.
Qualifications
A bachelor’s degree in electrical or electronic engineering, or a closely related discipline, with at least 15 years of relevant analog IC design experience; or a master’s degree in a relevant discipline with at least 11 years of relevant analog IC design experience.
Demonstrated hands-on design experience with bandgap references, LDOs, DC–DC regulators, oscillators and PLLs.
A proven track record of taking several products through the full development lifecycle to mass production, including silicon evaluation, debugging and production support.
Strong analog circuit fundamentals and practical expertise in transistor-level design, simulation, layout-dependent effects and post-layout verification.
Substantial architecture experience, with the ability to assess system-level requirements and translate them into robust, reusable analog IP solutions.
Experience engaging with product lines and translating competing product requirements into coherent IP specifications, development priorities and roadmaps.
Demonstrated experience mentoring junior engineers and providing technical leadership through design and architecture reviews.
Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts, present trade-offs and build alignment across engineering teams and product stakeholders.
A solid understanding of how AI can contribute to analog design and layout, including practical use cases, limitations and the need for independent engineering verification.
Desirable Experience
Experience in BCD technologies, particularly BCD65, and analog IP development for mixed-signal platforms.
Experience with supply and voltage monitoring, power-on reset, brownout detection and power or clock sequencing.
Experience defining reusable IP portfolios, configuration strategies and integration requirements across multiple product families.
Practical experience with scripting, design-flow automation or evaluation of AI-assisted engineering tools.
About Us

(Nasdaq: ON) is driving disruptive innovations to help build a better future. With a focus on automotive and industrial end-markets, the company is accelerating change in megatrends such as vehicle electrification and safety, sustainable energy grids, industrial automation, and 5G and cloud infrastructure. With a highly differentiated and innovative product portfolio, onsemi creates intelligent power and sensing technologies that solve the world’s most complex challenges and leads the way in creating a safer, cleaner, and smarter world.

jobs.desc:

Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.
We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.
Role description:
Our two-year Graduate GROW Programme supports your transition from student to professional, sitting along client work and real projects from day one. Each graduate’s journey is unique, shaped by their chosen specialism and the variety of projects they contribute to. You will build your technical expertise by contributing to meaningful client engagements and project work, whilst business acumen and professional skills will be developed through centrally delivered graduate cohort training. Although there are no formal rotations, graduates are encouraged and supported by their managers to proactively seek opportunities, to broaden their experience and support their development.
As an engineer joining GROW, you will be given the opportunity to specialise within your chosen discipline of engineering and we ensure you obtain the appropriate experiences that you need to become a technical expert. Being an Engineer at Arcadis is about applying a human filter to all your technical expertise and training, and making an impact through innovation and creativity. During this two-year programme you will develop core engineering and consulting techniques that can be applied while working with our clients in the UK and potentially even some of our international clients around the globe.
Role accountabilities:
Undertake engineering calculations and design tasks.
Assist in the preparation of drawings, BIM models, reports, and specifications.
Coordinate with other disciplines and project teams.
Participate in design reviews and QA/QC processes.
Support project delivery to agreed scope, schedule, and quality requirements.
Work towards professional accreditation (Engineers Ireland, ICE, IstructE).
Accepted Degrees:
Civil or Structural Engineering
Qualifications & Experience:
You will be graduating in 2027 or have recently graduated in 2025 or 2026, with at least a 2:2 in a relevant master's or bachelor's degree
You will demonstrate typical Arcadian skills including Resilience, Creativity, Analytical Thinking and being a Team Player
You will have excellent communication skills and the ability to use your technical knowledge to influence and consult stakeholders.
Willing to travel and stay away from home when required (where possible we embrace virtual working)
Why Arcadis?
We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.
You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.
Together, we can create a lasting legacy.
Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day which is why we take equality and inclusion seriously and hold ourselves to account for our actions. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We believe that by working together diverse people with different experiences develop the most innovative ideas. Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the heart of how we improve quality of life and we work closely with our people across six ED&I Workstreams: Age, Disability, Faith, Gender, LGBT+ and Race. jobs.title: Supply Chain Planner | Maternity Cover
jobs.desc:
Catalyx are seeking a Supply Chain Planner to join our team at our customer site in Cork for a 12-month maternity cover contract.
Who We Are
Catalyx is a machine vision and automation company that integrates technology and people to help global manufacturers and logistics companies achieve next-generation levels of quality and throughput. For over thirty years, the minds behind Catalyx have been at work maximizing operational processes across highly regulated industries by inventing new technology applications and supporting companies with technical experts. With 9 global offices, over 550 team members, and 3,000 projects under our belt (and counting), we have the capabilities and reach to solve unique process problems at scale – and the vision to keep doing what’s never been done before. For more information visit
www.catalyx.ai
.
Catalyx is a trusted partner in delivering world-class lifecycle services to regulated and high-risk end markets. With a relentless commitment to innovation and excellence, we partner with life science and other highly regulated organisations, to empower them to enhance efficiency, and drive success. As part of this commitment, we are continuously developing our on-site teams to support the advancement of customer operations.
Responsibilities
Work on supply chain problems of a diverse scope, where analysis of situations or data requires an evaluation of identifiable factors, establishment of root cause & implementation of corrective actions to meet business targets on OTIF, Inventory etc.
Work across organizational, cultural and geographic boundaries to optimize company strategic results within the supply chain function.
Introduce and integrate new technologies and\or new processes, as needed & support and develop inventory level tactics to support delivery of the business goals.
Provide input to more senior team members on planning and forecasting challenges to drive continuous improvement in standards.
Execute the planning and control of materials and finished goods to meet OTIF and distribution demand & Compile and analyse data to assist with decision-making.
Generate documents such as work orders, purchase orders, material transfer requests, or shipping documentation to support supply chain execution activities.
Track progress with department supervisors, readjust schedules and communicate changes according to production progress, change orders, manpower requirements, product availability or other conditions impacting timelines.
Use approved methods to make decisions in line with company goals and objectives, e.g. transfer or delivery of inventory, production and purchasing schedules, prioritisation of product release.
Develop and implement programs with Global Planning, CMO suppliers and\or internal cross-functional team members to support continuous improvement activities.
Requirements
The preferred candidate will have some years of relevant experience in related field and a BS or BA; or some years of relevant experience and a Master’s Degree.
Possess good planning and organizational skills coupled with strong communication, time management skills and an aptitude for working with computer systems to plan and manage supply chain requirements.
Demonstrate an in depth understanding and application of principles, concepts, practices, and standards along with an in depth knowledge of industry practices.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills and interpersonal skills, strong analytical skills and problem-solving capability.
Possess up-to-date knowledge of business operating systems, DRP, production scheduling, SAP\DB2\Access databases, and Excel, its uses and functions, and business need’s and developments.
Demonstrate the ability to develop solutions to a wide range of moderately complex problems, which require the regular use of ingenuity and innovation.
Proficient in ERP system software, with emphasis in the Operations\ Supply Chain functionality.
Knowledgeable in cGMP operations functionality.
Why Join Catalyx?
At Catalyx we understand that our people are our greatest asset. For this reason and many others, we take care of them. The team in Catalyx benefits from a Total Rewards package. This includes great personal benefits and professional growth opportunities.
Catalyx is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where all individuals are valued, respected, and supported. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of background, and strive to create a welcoming environment for everyone.
At Catalyx, we are committed to attracting the best global talent. We proudly support our international employees by offering assistance with Critical Skills Visa applications for eligible candidates.

Reporting to the CSA Department Manager, the Civil / Structural Engineer will be a member of the CSA Department supporting the delivery of civil and structural design services for major pharmaceutical and industrial clients. The role will have a predominantly civil engineering focus, with primary responsibility for underground drainage, underground electrical and utility services, site development works and drainage impact assessments. The Civil / Structural Engineer will also undertake structural engineering design and support structural project delivery as required.

Prepare engineering calculations, drainage impact assessments, reports, specifications, schedules and design documentation.

Design and coordinate underground water mains, electrical ducting, utility corridors and other buried services, including clash avoidance and interfaces with foundations and external works.

jobs.title: Hydro Team Member, General Operative (Lee Stations)
jobs.desc:
Position Description
A vacancy exists for the position of Hydro Team Member, Lee Generating Stations.
Built between 1952 and 1957, Lee Generating Stations joined the schemes on the rivers Shannon, Erne, and Liffey to become ESB’s fourth major hydroelectric development. This involved creating two reservoirs in the Lee Valley, which:
cover an area of 14km² and
have a storage capacity of 45 million cubic meters.
We have been generating electricity on the River Lee since 1957. Our station has a combined generating capacity of 27 MW. The stations engineering, Maintenance and Operations teams play a pivotal role in ensuring the safe operation of the station and that commercial / technical performance is optimised at Inniscarra. Both units use Voith turbines with Brown Boveri generators, which operate under an average head of 30m. Carrigadrohid has one generating unit (Voith turbine/Siemens generator) with a capacity of 8 MW, operating under an average head of 13m. Lee Stations are a high efficiency producer of renewable energy and are part of ESB’s goal to reach Net Zero by 2040.
As a member of the station team, the Hydro Team Member will be required to work across all functional areas including maintenance, operations, technical services, facilities, civil, procurement and dam safety, supervision, and contractor management. The successful candidate will be required to work to the level of their competence to carry out their duties. They will provide support to other teams and projects. Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively with others is required. The successful candidate will give and receive training as defined by plant management to attain and maintain competencies.
As ESB transitions to Net Zero by 2040, working in Lee Hydro Generating Station offers a unique opportunity to significantly impact ESB’s vision.
Key Responsibilities
Duties of the role include but may not be limited to:
Delivering and supporting work across all areas of the station.
Working safely, flexibly and to competence, as part of the overall team.
General Site / Facilities Services and Maintenance works e.g., concreting works, property repairs, equipment checks, waste management etc.
Fixed and mobile plant operation, equipment checks, deliveries and collections.
Assisting Operations and Maintenance Hydro Team members
Witnessing gate movements during water control operations.
General Administration duties including ordering, goods receipting, etc.
Ordering of equipment and stores items, stock checks
Taking instrument measurements and entering them into computerised dam monitoring systems.
Use of ESB computer systems for maintenance and administration duties.
Carry out authorized roles under the safety rules as required.
The successful candidate will be required on occasions to have flexible working hours including weekend and night working and be available for call-outs.
Experience And Qualifications
Essential
Health, Safety & Environment (HSE) Awareness
Hold a full valid B driving license
Applicants must be proficient in the use of computer systems (Word, Excel etc.)
Excellent communication skills.
Desirable
Experience in industrial plants and /or construction or building maintenance works.
Relevant CSCS tickets and qualifications
Awareness of Safe System of Work
Experience using SAP or other procurement systems.
Experience using Maintenance Management Systems.
Location

jobs.title: Security Researcher - SAP
jobs.desc:
Summary
Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization. IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.
In a fast-evolving digital world, our team seeks a Security Researcher with an offensive security mindset to tackle emerging cyber threats within Apple’s critical ERP environment. You will play a pivotal role in safeguarding our dynamic, hybrid enterprise systems, which underpin Apple’s supply chain, treasury, and customer experiences. This unique opportunity focuses on shifting security left by relentlessly pursuing and identifying vulnerabilities early and often within the development lifecycle. You will apply cutting-edge offensive security techniques, code analysis, and penetration testing to generate meaningful data that drives the evolution of secure development standards. If you possess the necessary offensive security skills, an insatiable desire to find vulnerabilities in sophisticated systems, a passion for ethical hacking, and a strong curiosity for how enterprise systems function, we would love to meet you!
Description
Conduct advanced offensive security testing across Apple’s hybrid SAP landscape, including: Manual penetration testing of custom ABAP & Java applications, SAP Fiori apps, web applications, APIs, and mobile interfaces.
Vulnerability research and testing within SAP S/4HANA, ECC, BTP services, Ariba, Commerce Cloud, Signavio, LeanIX, and other integrated cloud-native systems.
Security assessments of underlying infrastructure and cloud environments supporting SAP. Perform deep-dive source code reviews of sophisticated applications to identify security flaws and architectural weaknesses.
Develop custom scripts, tools, and proof-of-concept exploits to augment penetration testing activities, automate vulnerability discovery, and demonstrate impact.
Proactively identify and research emerging threats and attack vectors relevant to enterprise systems and the SAP ecosystem.
Document findings in high-quality, actionable reports and presentations, clearly communicating technical vulnerabilities, their business impact, and recommended remediations to engineering teams across the organization.
Collaborate closely with engineering and development teams to provide security advice, improve secure coding practices, and integrate security early into the development lifecycle (shift-left). Assemble and analyze threat & vulnerability data to highlight issues and trends, and author enhanced development standards and security requirements.
Contribute to the team’s security knowledge base, sharing expertise, developing technical documentation, and shaping testing methodologies.
Continuously learn and develop expertise in offensive security techniques and the intricacies of the SAP ecosystem.
Minimum Qualifications
Experience in offensive security, penetration testing, vulnerability research, or a related field (internships, research projects, open-source contributions, CTF participation, or bug bounty success are highly valued).
In-depth knowledge of web application security, API security, system and infrastructure security, and common attack techniques.
Ability to read, understand, and find vulnerabilities in sophisticated codebases (e.g., ABAP, Java, JavaScript, Go).
Proficiency in at least one scripting or programming language (e.g., Python, PowerShell, Bash, Go, Ruby, JavaScript (Node.js)) for security automation and tool development.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, with the ability to analyze complex challenges and produce creative solutions.
Preferred Qualifications
Relevant offensive security certifications (e.g., OSCP, OSWE, OSWP, eJPT) are highly regarded.
Experience with CTFs, hacking labs, bug bounty programs, or public security research/CVEs.
Knowledge of cloud architecture and security principles (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP, SAP BTP).
Familiarity with modern cybersecurity concepts including AI/ML applications in security, cryptography, and prompt engineering for security tasks.
An insatiable curiosity for how complex enterprise systems work, with a mandatory desire to learn and understand the SAP ecosystem. (No prior SAP expertise required, but a strong aptitude and willingness to dive deep into this domain is essential).
Proficiency in MacOS and other Unix-based systems.
Experience with or a strong interest in learning ABAP is a significant plus.

Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates to help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities.
Strategy Consulting
Responding to global challenges requires rapid adaptation and transformation of the built environment. Our Strategy Consulting team brings together four core teams – Strategy & Transformation, Strategic Communications & Engagement, Data Insights & AI, and Data Advisory – who work together to help our clients navigate and deliver change.
As part of our growth ambitions, we are recruiting a motivated and driven graduate to join our Strategy & Transformation team. Find out more about Strategy Consulting at Arup.
The Opportunity
You’ll join a multidisciplinary team that helps clients navigate complex challenges, identify opportunities and deliver sustainable, transformational change. Our work spans infrastructure, transport, sustainability, digital transformation, organisational change and business strategy – so no two projects look the same.
From day one, you’ll learn how to design strategies, turn data into insight and communicate with stakeholders in a way that moves people to act. Initially a broad role, it gives you exposure across the wider Strategy Consulting team, with the opportunity to specialise over time – in strategy and transformation, communications and engagement, or a blend of both.
As a Graduate Consultant, you will but not limited to:
Research industry trends, market dynamics and emerging issues to inform strategy development.
Analyse qualitative and quantitative data to uncover opportunities and shape recommendations.
Help develop and implement strategic, organisational change and innovation initiatives that deliver real value to clients.
Prepare reports, presentations and business cases that summarise findings, recommendations and next steps.
Support stakeholder engagement and strategic communications, including workshops, consultations and client meetings.
Help coordinate project activities, timelines and deliverables.
Build strong client relationships through regular communication and responsiveness.
Collaborate with colleagues across disciplines to solve complex challenges across the built environment.
Does this role inspire you?
We’re looking for graduates who are passionate about sustainable development and bring a curious, problem-solving and innovative mindset.

A Level 8 (Bachelor’s) Degree Or Above In a Relevant Discipline. We Also Welcome Candidates Who Hold, Or Are Pursuing, a Master’s Or PhD. Relevant Disciplines Include, But Are Not Limited To
Business, Commerce and Economics
Management, Strategy and Management Consulting
Engineering
Psychology (including Organisational Psychology), Organisational Behaviour and Change Management
Communications, Social Sciences and Public Policy
Business and Data Analytics
Sustainability, Urban Planning and Transport Planning
Strong research, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to turn complex information into clear, compelling insights.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including presentation and report writing.
Adaptability and an appetite to learn on the job.
Strong professional acumen and work ethic.
The ability to work as part of a team and independently, across multiple projects.
A sustainability mindset, with an awareness of the economic, environmental and societal challenges facing organisations.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Excel, Word and Teams).
An interest in infrastructure, transport, urban, sustainability and regional development.
Exposure to any of the following would be a bonus, but is not essential: Power BI, Miro, data visualisation, workshop facilitation, process mapping, business case development, change management methods, or AI-enabled tools such as Microsoft Copilot.

Changemakers: A passion for sustainable development and creating a better world is key.
Innovative minds: We’re looking for critical thinkers who embrace new ideas and challenge the status quo.
Growth seekers: You have a growth mindset, always eager to learn and explore new ways of working.
Adaptable adventurers: You’re ready to take on any challenge that comes your way.

At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.
Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.
We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling permanent members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
In Ireland, our permanent members also receive private medical insurance allowances, life assurance and income protection cover.

Purpose-driven work: Join an employee-owned team tackling climate, biodiversity and social challenges, aligned with the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals.
Create remarkable outcomes: We trust you to explore challenges, drive change and create lasting outcomes for our clients, climate and communities.
Inclusive culture: Your unique perspective matters. We celebrate diversity and foster a supportive, social environment where everyone belongs.
Career growth: Grow your skills through innovative projects, training and mentoring in a supportive environment. We invest in your future.
Work-life balance: Our hybrid model and flexible approach to working help you balance work with your life, alongside the needs of our clients and communities.
Before you apply
To be considered for a graduate opportunity, your application must include a copy of your academic transcript, and you must:
Have no more than 12 months of full-time experience in a comparable role.
Have recently graduated, or be on track to graduate, from your most recent degree (related to this role) before your start date.

12 November 2026

Highly proficient in automation scripting using Python, TCL, or Perl.
Strong knowledge of the complete ASIC design flow (RTL-to-GDS).

STA Design Engineer / Static Timing Analysis / STA / Timing Closure / ASIC Design / SOC / PrimeTime / Tempus / Timing ECO / PPA Optimization / Gate-Level Netlist / Python / TCL / Physical Design / RTL / Synthesis / Semiconductor / High-Performance Cores

jobs.title: Threat Researcher 2
jobs.desc:
#RunwiththePack
At Arctic Wolf, we’re on a mission to
end cyber risk
.
We are a global leader in security operations, helping organizations stay resilient against evolving cyber threats through industry-leading security operations, threat intelligence, and a people-first approach to cybersecurity.
More than 3,000 Pack members across the world work together every day to protect our customers and empower security teams with new levels of speed, accuracy, and intelligence at scale. What sets us apart is our relentless focus on our customers, innovation at scale, and a collaborative culture where talented people can do meaningful work that truly makes a difference.
We’re constantly looking for talented people to join the Pack and help us take our performance to the next level.
About The Position
About the Team:
Arctic Wolf Threat Content Team is the owner and intellectual author of the telemetry and detection rules of our Aurora Focus (EDR) product, part of Aurora Endpoint Defense.
Our Team started only 4 years ago in BlackBerry-Cylance. Since then we have developed many internal tools to streamline our daily tasks, defined work standards and how to create content (detection/telemetry rules), and high fidelity content (fine tune processes, reduce f+), created quality assurance processes (Unit Test, Regression and E2E Testing), communication channels with other areas of Threat Intel and Security Services, without neglecting our main mission which is end cyber risk.
About The Role And Responsibilities
Analyse, research, and develop new content for Aurora Focus, applying MITRE ATT&CK framework.
Convert investigations performed by our Threat Teams: TRI\ATD\CTI into new content (detection/telemetry rules).
Customer Escalation (BFD), collaborate with Security Services teams on investigations regarding emerging threats, to generate new detection rules.
Fine tuning: determining true threats or false positives, and providing solutions, like exclusions, logic change or decreasing severity.
Python scripting to automate new internal tools or projects.
Ability to effectively manage multiple tasks simultaneously; coordinating and ensuring scheduled goals are met.
Maintain documentation up to date: about a new tool or process we add.
Run regression and end-2-end testing
Push production releases, and notification emails.
Participate in Purple Teaming exercises
Generate metrics over Databricks Dashboard.
Deliver regular threat briefing presentations to internal & external stakeholders on topics ranging from threat actor campaign activity, novel TTPs, and emerging malware or exploits
Utilize best practices for threat research and documentation and deliver high-quality detection rules.
About You
Relevant experience in a professional setting for threat intelligence or threat research roles, 2+ years.
Experience with applying the MITRE ATT&CK framework to intelligence products and associated depth of analysis for each TTP and threat actor represented in this body of knowledge
Experience analysing application and infrastructure telemetry (application logs, network flow logs, audit logs, metrics, core dumps, etc.)
Experience analysing and deriving intelligence from phishing and malware campaigns, vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, supply chain attacks, and Data breaches
Understanding of threat protection/detection tooling/stacks: SIEM, XDR/EDR
Experience working with Python scripts.
Understand Json format and regex usage.
Linux and MacOS Terminal usage
Basic .sh/.bat scripting knowledge
Windows sysinternals
Experience using Git repositories (GitHub, Git Bash, GitLab)
Experience using Virtual Machines (VMware workstation)
SQL Knowledge, Databricks is a plus.
Lolbins/Lolbas Knowledge
Sigma Rules Knowledge
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Resourceful self-starter with a positive, can-do attitude
Nice To Have
Experience with Agile Methodology
Experience using Elastic search, Kibana or Grafana.
You have delivered presentations on cybersecurity or cyber threat intelligence at industry conferences or meetups
You have participated in sharing of threat intelligence through ISACs, Trust Groups, intelligence partnerships, or via other open communities
CISSP, OSCP, GCTI or other relevant certifications are a plus
Benefits
All wolves receive compelling compensation and benefits packages, including:
Equity for all employees
28 days annual leave, 10 public holidays, and paid volunteering days off
Comprehensive private benefits plan including medical, optical and dental, life insurance and group income protection
Pension Plan with employer contribution
Robust Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with mental health service
Employee Discount Program with Beneplace
Security Requirements
At Arctic Wolf, protecting our people, customers, and data is fundamental to how we operate. All employees are expected to uphold our commitment to security, privacy, and compliance by following internal information security policies, standards, and controls designed to safeguard the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of business, customer, employee, and other confidential information and to support compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
Depending on the role and where permitted by applicable law, employment may be subject to background verification and additional regulatory, security, or compliance requirements, including obligations related to data protection and export control laws, and authorization requirements where applicable.
Base Salary
The base salary range for this job family is 48,000 to 105,000 EUR annually. This range reflects the base pay the company reasonably expects to offer for this position, aligned to the broader job family base pay structure. Actual base pay may vary based on skills, experience, and location, including job family level. In addition to base pay, Arctic Wolf offers variable incentive compensation, new hire equity grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere.
