Whilst you will have a core role, you may be asked to support your colleagues by helping in other departments.
You will need
Able to give great, natural customer service by proactively smiling, greeting, acknowledging and helping customers.
Works hard for customers, your team and your department.
You are able to prioritise to ensure anything you do is right for our customers.
Adaptable and resilient to meet the ever changing demands of our business.
You must be able to follow instructions either verbal or written.
You are reliable and a good timekeeper.
You must be smart and tidy at all times.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren't limited to:
Competitive Salary
Bonus Scheme*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2nd Clubcard available.*
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer's favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move. Our core purpose is "Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day". Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers. It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children's Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings. We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That's why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/

jobs.title: Monetization Specialist – Expansion (Recovery & Involuntary Churn)
jobs.desc:
Role Summary
We are looking for a Monetization Specialist – Expansion to reduce involuntary churn and improve failed-payment (FTC) recovery for McAfee's subscription base. Sitting on the Expansion team, you will own the strategy and execution of messaging, product, and payment enhancements that keep paying customers subscribed when a payment fails, or before it does.
This is a hybrid role based in either our Ireland or Spain hubs. You may be required to travel to the US as needed; when not onsite, you will work remotely from your home location.
Position Details
About The Role
As a Monetization Specialist – Expansion, you will support initiatives that protect recurring revenue by preventing and recovering failed payments across the customer lifecycle. You will work across three levers: messaging enhancements (pre-dunning, dunning, grace period, expiration, and reactivation journeys), product enhancements (in-product experiences that surface and resolve payment issues), and payment enhancements (retry logic, payment method updates, and billing flows). You will partner closely with Payments, Martech, Product, Analytics, Engineering, and Lifecycle Marketing to turn insights into tested, measurable improvements.
Key Responsibilities
Own the FTC recovery strategy and roadmap across messaging, product, and payment enhancements, with clear targets for recovery rate, churn reduction, and retained revenue.
Improve recovery journey performance through higher testing velocity, messaging optimization, and disciplined experimentation across email, in-app, push, SMS, and landing pages.
Develop prevention programs that reach customers at risk of involuntary churn before a payment failure occurs (for example, expiring cards and payment method health).
Partner with Payments and Engineering to identify and implement payment enhancements such as retry logic, payment method update flows, and billing experience improvements.
Partner with Product and Martech to deliver new recovery capabilities and customer touchpoints, including in-product experiences.
Identify friction points and segmentation opportunities to personalize recovery and prevention experiences.
Build and maintain a prioritized testing roadmap, sizing opportunities and sequencing initiatives by expected impact.
Establish performance reporting with Analytics, and deliver recommendations and learnings in recurring business reviews and monetization readouts.
About You
5+ years of experience in subscription businesses, CRM, lifecycle marketing, retention, or monetization roles.
Hands-on experience reducing involuntary churn or improving failed-payment recovery.
Working knowledge of payments and billing, including payment failure causes, retry strategies, and recovery stages such as pre-dunning, dunning, grace period, expiration, and reactivation.
Experience with CRM and customer engagement platforms (Braze preferred), including segmentation, journey orchestration, experimentation, and measurement.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to size opportunities, prioritize, and turn data into an actionable testing roadmap.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally with Payments, Martech, Product, Analytics, Engineering, and Marketing teams.
Comfortable managing multiple workstreams while maintaining speed of execution and focus on business impact.
Experience in consumer technology, cybersecurity, telecom, streaming, media, fintech, or SaaS subscription businesses is a plus.
Company Overview
McAfee is a leader in personal security for consumers. Focused on protecting people, not just devices, McAfee consumer solutions adapt to users’ needs in an always online world, empowering them to live securely through integrated, intuitive solutions that protects their families and communities with the right security at the right moment.

Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world.

Experience working within and supporting the configuration of CDE platforms, preferably Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) and/or Bentley ProjectWise.

Strong communication and organisational skills, with the ability to facilitate coordination activities and engage effectively with multidisciplinary project teams.

A qualification in BIM or Information Management
Experience using Autodesk Revit on infrastructure projects
Experience using Autodesk Infraworks for early-stage site conceptual design and visualization
Knowledge of Autodesk Navisworks for model federation, coordination, clash detection, issue review and construction sequencing.

Awareness of BIM-related project risks, capability assessments, mobilisation activities and information delivery reporting.
Experience supporting, mentoring or training colleagues in BIM authoring tools, coordination processes, CDE workflows and project standards.

jobs.desc:
Mechanical DesignerAbout The Company
Our client is a leading engineering and manufacturing organisation supplying innovative equipment and solutions to the biopharmaceutical manufacturing industry. With decades of industry experience, the company provides a comprehensive range of engineering, design, manufacturing, commissioning, qualification and service solutions.
Their expertise includes process and equipment engineering, site services, bioreactors and fermenters, filtration and chromatography systems, preparation and hold systems, and cleaning and sterilisation equipment.
The company is continuing to grow its design team and is now seeking an experienced Mechanical Designer to join their team.
The Role
Reporting to the Design Team Leader, the Mechanical Designer will be responsible for the design, development and release of engineering deliverables for pilot and commercial-scale biopharmaceutical manufacturing equipment.
The role will focus primarily on the design of pressure vessel assemblies, fluid and gas handling systems, and motorised agitation systems, using Autodesk Inventor and AutoCAD.
This is a detail-focused role that will require the successful candidate to develop a strong understanding of ASME/BPE bioprocessing equipment standards, while working closely with engineering, project management, manufacturing and customers.
Key Responsibilities
Design, develop and maintain detailed engineering drawings and assembly documentation.
Review and interpret customer specifications, requirements and technical documentation.
Produce and maintain 3D models, detail drawings, spool drawings and Bills of Materials (BOMs).
Create and maintain piping arrangement drawings, including top assembly and piping modules, using P&IDs and customer specifications.
Design and maintain agitation system assemblies.
Develop and maintain component BOM documentation.
Prepare and process Engineering Change Notices (ECNs) in line with company procedures and best practices.
Maintain accurate project files and design documentation.
Participate in design reviews with internal teams, customers and project management.
Record design review actions and ensure required changes are communicated effectively to the project team.
Provide technical and manufacturing support relating to released designs and documentation.
Produce accurate as-built documentation for Quality and project requirements.
Work collaboratively with Project Engineering, Project Management, Manufacturing and other internal departments.
Manage priorities effectively to meet project deadlines and customer commitments.
Travel domestically and internationally when required.
Undertake additional project and design-related duties as required.
Requirements
Level 6 qualification in Computer Aided Design and Drafting (CADD) or equivalent.
At least 1 year of postgraduate experience in drafting and design.
Experience with 3D parametric CAD software.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Word and Excel.
Strong understanding of drafting standards, design fundamentals and fabrication processes.
Excellent attention to detail.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Good organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a collaborative team.
Willingness and ability to travel when required.
Desirable Experience
1–2 years' experience in a related engineering or manufacturing environment using 3D parametric CAD software.
Experience carrying a design project from initial concept through to production.
Experience preparing and processing ECNs, BOMs and technical design documentation.
Previous experience using Autodesk Inventor, particularly Routed Systems.
Experience with Autodesk AutoCAD 2D/3D.
Experience using ERP systems for item and BOM creation; experience with Syteline would be advantageous.
Knowledge or experience of ASME/BPE bioprocessing equipment standards.
What We're Looking For
The ideal candidate will be a technically minded and detail-oriented Mechanical Designer who enjoys working on complex engineering projects. You will have a strong interest in 3D design and the ability to interpret technical requirements and translate them into accurate manufacturing-ready designs.
You will be comfortable working in a customer-focused environment, collaborating with multiple departments and taking ownership of your design work from concept through to production.
For more information please call Christina Keating on 0
21 494 4871 or email christina.keating@cpl.ie

We are looking for an enthusiastic Drone Remote Pilot to join our growing Drone as a Service (DaaS) team. You will operate uncrewed aircraft on behalf of clients across a wide range of sectors — including construction, energy and utilities, telecoms, infrastructure, agriculture, real estate, surveying and insurance — capturing high-quality aerial data for surveys, inspections, mapping and bespoke projects.
This is an entry-level position ideal for someone who is passionate about drones and aerial technology, eager to learn, and ready to build a long-term career in the commercial UAS industry. jobs.title: Procurement Advisory Work Placement
jobs.desc:
See it differently
You see the world through a unique lens and that’s exactly what we need. We embrace how you see things differently – it’s essential for creating a sustainable future.
Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates and students who help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities.
The Opportunity
As a Procurement Advisory work placement student at Arup, you will:
Assist senior team members in delivering construction projects dealing with payment certificates and claims.
Assist senior team members in the preparation of bills of quantities, ensuring compliance with required method of measurement.
Be proactive in communicating and working with the direct team as well as Arup colleagues from various disciplines for the successful delivery of tasks.
Follow instructions and/or use own initiative to achieve designated tasks in a timely manner.
Understand the required outputs/deliverables of a project or assignment and work efficiently to deliver them.
Develop relationships with colleagues, always being professional, presentable and articulate.
Adopt a flexible approach to working, supporting multiple teams across the buildings and infrastructure sectors
Is this role right for you?
We're looking for students who are currently working towards RICS accredited, surveying-based degree. We also value students who are:
Proactive, motivated and enthusiastic. Able to apply their own initiative to undertake tasks independently.
A team player, who can adopt flexible working practices to support the needs of the business.
Articulate, with both excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Logical in their approach to tasks, with the ability to interpret, understand and analyse data.
Output focused, always working with the objective in mind.
Commercially astute with strong numerical skills, demonstrating an attention to detail.
Proficient with Microsoft Office products and ideally Cost X (Although not necessary).
Alongside your degree, we look for the following core attributes;
Changemakers: A passion for sustainable development and creating a better world is key.
Innovative minds: We’re looking for critical thinkers who embrace new ideas and challenge the status quo.
Growth seekers: You have a growth mindset, always eager to learn and explore new ways of working.
Adaptable adventurers: You’re ready to take on any challenge that comes your way.
Advert Closing Date:
12 November 2026
Please note, in the event of high applicant volume, this role may be closed ahead of the advertised closing date. Early application is recommended.
What we offer you
At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.
Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.
We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling permanent members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
We take an approach to flexible working that supports the diversity and wellbeing of our graduates.
Different people, shared values
Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas - this drives our excellence.
Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. jobs.title: Graduate Program Associate - Manufacturing Technical Services
jobs.desc:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.
Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.
We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.
Job Description
Graduate Program Associate - Manufacturing Technical Services
2026 Intake, start date late November or early December
About Gilead
Gilead Sciences, Inc. is a research-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops and commercialises innovative medicines in areas of unmet medical need. With each new discovery and investigational drug candidate, we seek to improve the care of patients living with life-threatening diseases around the world. Gilead’s therapeutic areas of focus include HIV/AIDS, liver diseases, cancer and inflammation, and serious respiratory and cardiovascular conditions.
The Position
We have an opportunity for a Graduate to join our team for a 2 year programme, working within the Development and Technical Services function and rotating to key relevant areas as below. Throughout this time, the successful candidate will be developed and mentored to aid your on the job learning.
The Development and Technical Services Department at our Manufacturing facility in Cork, support the introduction of new products to the site, the management of the lifecycle of products and supports the manufacture of Gilead products at third party manufacturing facilities.
As a Graduate within our Development and Technical Services Department, you will have the opportunity to develop fundamental skills related to the manufacture of Oral Solid Dose Products including drug product formulation and process development, Quality by Design (QbD), oversight of GMP drug product manufacturing, global regulatory requirements and the application of operation excellence methodologies to problem solving and process improvement projects.
The role offers potential development opportunities to the candidate in the following related functions: Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality Assurance and Validation.
Key Responsibilities
The successful candidate will rotate into key areas, building responsibility and experience in the below:
Supports the technical transfer of new products to site.
Contributes to the completion of all technical support activities related to maintaining commercial product supplies.
Contributes to and may lead complex processes across functions and interacts effectively with the other team members to ensure product meets regulatory, performance and cost requirements.
Contributes to and may lead technical investigations of process deviations and assessment of their impact on product quality.
Defines requirements for and reviews master batch records.
Conducts non-routine analysis of raw materials, intermediates, and finished product samples.
Troubleshoots instrumentation such as particle size analyzers or other measurement devices used in material characterization.
Assists in the training of manufacturing technicians as needed.
Applies knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs).
Writes and executes SOPs, protocols and reports.
Supports yield improvements on site.
Supports qualification of new excipients and APIs to site.
Identifies new technologies to support site requirements.
Knowledge, Experience & Skills
A minimum 2.1 level 8 degree in a related area such as Science, Process, Chemical or Biopharmaceutical Engineering.
Good problem solving and attention to detail.
Highly adaptable and displaying good initiative.
Strong communication, team player and ability to build effective relationships.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
Gilead Core Values
Integrity (Doing What’s Right)
Teamwork (Working Together)
Excellence (Being Your Best)
Accountability (Taking Personnel Responsibility)
Inclusion (Encouraging Diversity)
Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO)

Except if otherwise provided by applicable law, all employment actions relating to issues such as compensation, benefits, transfers, layoffs, returns from layoffs, company-sponsored training, education assistance, social and recreational programs are administered on a non-discriminatory basis (i.e. without regard to protected characteristics or prohibited grounds, which may include an individual’s gender, race, color, national origin, ancestry, religion, creed, physical or mental disability, marital status, sexual orientation, medical condition, veteran status, and age, unless such protection is prohibited by federal, state, municipal, provincial, local or other applicable laws). Astellas is a global life sciences company committed to turning innovative science into VALUE for patients. We provide transformative therapies in disease areas that include oncology, ophthalmology, urology, immunology and women's health. Through our research and development programs, we are pioneering new healthcare solutions for diseases with high unmet medical need. Learn more at Astellas.com .

jobs.title: Deal Management Analyst - Graduate
jobs.desc:
Cohesity is the leader in AI-powered data security. Over 13,600 enterprise customers, including over 85 of the Fortune 100 and nearly 70% of the Global 500, rely on Cohesity to strengthen their resilience while providing Gen AI insights into their vast amounts of data. Formed from the combination of Cohesity with Veritas’ enterprise data protection business, the company’s solutions secure and protect data on-premises, in the cloud, and at the edge. Backed by NVIDIA, IBM, HPE, Cisco, AWS, Google Cloud, and others, Cohesity is headquartered in Santa Clara, CA, with offices around the globe.
We’ve been named a Leader by multiple analyst firms and have been globally recognized for Innovation, Product Strength, and Simplicity in Design , and our culture.
Want to join the leader in AI-powered data security?
Ready to turn your degree into a career you'll be excited about? Join Cohesity and become part of a team that helps power the commercial engine of one of the world's leading AI-powered data security companies!
As a
Deal Management Analyst Graduate
, you'll gain real-world business experience from day one, working on customer deals, collaborating with teams across the globe, and learning how commercial decisions drive company growth. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside Sales, Finance, Operations, and Strategy teams, gaining exposure to everything from pricing and forecasting to process improvement and business analytics.
This role is perfect for graduates who are curious, analytical, enjoy problem-solving, and want to build a strong foundation in business and technology. You'll be supported by experienced mentors, encouraged to share your ideas, and given the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while developing valuable skills that will accelerate your career.
HOW WILL YOU SPEND YOUR TIME?
Learn how customer deals are structured and support the review of pricing, discounts, commercial terms, and approvals.
Partner with Sales, Finance, Revenue Operations, and other teams to help move opportunities through the sales cycle.
Gain exposure to high-value commercial deals and learn how successful businesses balance growth, profitability, and customer needs.
Participate in forecasting discussions and develop an understanding of how sales pipelines translate into revenue.
Analyse deal trends and business data to help identify opportunities for improvement and smarter decision-making.
Support sales teams by responding to inquiries and helping solve commercial and operational challenges.
Contribute to projects focused on process improvement, automation, and operational excellence.
Test and provide feedback on new tools, systems, and enhancements that improve the deal management experience.
Create reports and insights that help leaders make informed business decisions.
Collaborate with colleagues around the world and gain exposure to a fast-paced, global technology business.
WE'D LOVE TO TALK TO YOU IF YOU HAVE MANY OF THE FOLLOWING:
You're graduating in 2027 with a degree in Business, Commerce, Finance, Economics, Management, Analytics, BIS, Data Analytics, or a related field.
You're excited by the idea of combining business, technology, and problem-solving.
You enjoy working with data and turning information into insights.
You're naturally curious and eager to learn how things work and how they can be improved.
You enjoy collaborating with others and building strong relationships across different teams.
You have strong communication skills and can explain ideas clearly and confidently.
You're organised, proactive, and comfortable managing multiple priorities.
You enjoy tackling challenges and finding creative solutions.
You have experience using technology and AI tools to work smarter and enhance productivity.
You bring a positive attitude, a growth mindset, and a willingness to step outside your comfort zone.
Fluency in English is required; additional European languages are a plus.

Review employment-related policies and contractual documentation.
Manage external employment counsel where necessary.

Advise on confidentiality, proprietary information, and trade secret protection.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with external partners, distributors, manufacturers, and consultants to ensure contractual and regulatory compliance.
Build strong working relationships across Evumed's European operations.
Provide practical legal guidance, training and mentoring to commercial and functional teams, supporting sound commercial judgement and effective risk management.
Process Development & Continuous Improvement

Support digitalisation and automation initiatives within legal and compliance functions.

jobs.desc:
Mechanical Design Engineer
Location:
Cork, Ireland
Job Type:
Permanent | Full-time
The Opportunity
Occupli is partnering with an established engineering business specialising in the design and manufacture of bespoke capital equipment for the pharmaceutical and life sciences sectors.
We are seeking a
Mechanical Design Engineer
to join an experienced engineering team, contributing to the design and development of complex, engineered equipment from initial concept through to manufacture, assembly and testing.
This is an opportunity for an engineer who enjoys combining practical mechanical design expertise with problem-solving, technical collaboration and involvement in the full project lifecycle.
The Role
Working as part of a multidisciplinary project team, you will translate technical and customer requirements into detailed mechanical designs and manufacturing documentation, ensuring solutions are technically sound, practical to manufacture and delivered in line with project specifications.
You will also work closely with production, fabrication, automation, procurement and project management teams, providing technical support throughout the design and manufacturing process.
Key Responsibilities
Develop 3D models and 2D engineering drawings for specialist mechanical equipment using CAD software.
Interpret technical specifications and customer User Requirement Specifications (URS).
Produce detailed engineering drawings, general arrangements, component details, bills of materials and manufacturing documentation.
Undertake mechanical concept and detailed design, including sheet metal components and fabrication drawings.
Apply Design for Manufacture (DFM) principles to ensure designs are practical, efficient and cost-effective to produce.
Provide technical support to fabrication and assembly teams, resolving design queries and addressing manufacturing challenges.
Participate in engineering design reviews and coordinate technical documentation for customer approval.
Collaborate with project managers and multidisciplinary engineering teams to achieve project milestones and delivery schedules.
Support supplier identification, component selection and procurement activities.
Manage engineering design changes and associated technical documentation.
Contribute to Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) activities.
Skills & Experience
To be considered, you should have:
A degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline.
A minimum of three years' experience in mechanical design, ideally involving machinery, specialist equipment or engineered systems.
Strong 3D CAD capability, with experience in Solid Edge, SolidWorks, Autodesk Inventor or comparable software.
Good knowledge of sheet metal design, fabrication and flat pattern development.
Experience producing detailed engineering and manufacturing drawings, including general arrangements, component details and assembly documentation.
An understanding of Design for Manufacture and the practical requirements of fabrication and machining.
Experience working with technical specifications and managing multiple engineering deliverables.
Good communication and organisational skills, with the ability to work effectively across engineering, production and customer-facing teams.
Additional experience that would be advantageous:
Exposure to pharmaceutical or life sciences equipment manufacturing.
Familiarity with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and GMP-related engineering documentation.
Knowledge of relevant machinery safety standards and regulatory requirements, including ATEX, CE and UL.
Experience with Factory Acceptance Testing and Site Acceptance Testing.
The Opportunity
Join a technically specialised engineering environment where you will have the opportunity to work on complex equipment, contribute to engineering solutions and see your designs progress from concept through to physical manufacture.
If you are a Mechanical Design Engineer looking for your next opportunity within a specialist engineering and manufacturing environment, we would welcome a confidential conversation.
Apply through Occupli to find out more.

jobs.title: Kinisla Research & Development Graduate 2027
jobs.desc:
Start Your Career with Kinisla!
Join the Kinisla Graduate Programme in a permanent, full-time role designed for ambitious graduates who aspire to become future senior leaders in our business. This is more than an entry-level graduate job: it is a structured two-year leadership development programme commencing September 2027. It combines formal learning, hands-on operational experience, meaningful projects, mentoring across the business. From day one, you will be challenged to build the commercial, operational and leadership capabilities needed to grow your career with Kinisla.
Assessment centres will take place during the week commencing 18 January 2027. As part of the selection process, you must be available to attend in person during that week.
Working in Research & Development at Kinisla:
At Kinisla, our Research & Development function is rooted in the practical application of dairy science and innovation. As a graduate, you will join a team that combines scientific expertise with commercial insight to develop and improve products that make a real impact. You will contribute to live projects from day one—whether enhancing functionality, improving nutrition or supporting customer innovation through tailored dairy applications—while collaborating with teams across operations, supply chain, quality and commercial.
On our two-year programme, you will have the opportunity to build experience across the Kinisla business, gaining exposure to different areas and developing a broader understanding of how we operate. Your responsibilities may include:
Supporting the development and optimisation of dairy products from concept through to commercialisation across categories such as cheese, spreads and fermented dairy
Collaborating with operations, quality and supply chain teams to ensure product feasibility and manufacturing readiness
Conducting bench-scale and pilot trials to improve product performance, shelf life and sensory attributes, with a focus on nutrition and sustainability
Applying food science principles to enhance functionality and meet evolving customer and regulatory requirements
Participating in customer projects and technical requests, including troubleshooting, reformulation and scale-up activities
Maintaining accurate technical documentation and formulation records to support product launches and continuous improvement
Engaging with commercial teams to understand market needs and translate them into viable product solutions
Building a strong understanding of Kinisla's product portfolio and its application across retail and foodservice channels.
Developing Kinisla's Future Leaders:
Our Graduate Programme is designed to accelerate your development and prepare you for increasing responsibility and future leadership opportunities at Kinisla. You will benefit from:
A permanent role with structured development over two years
Off-the-job learning modules, mentoring and group projects
Hands-on responsibility and meaningful project work from day one
Opportunities to build a broad network across Kinisla
By the end of the programme, you will have built strong Research & Development expertise, a broad understanding of the business and the leadership foundations to progress towards more senior roles at Kinisla.
Do You Have What It Takes?
You are on track to achieve, or have recently completed, a degree with at least a 2:1 classification in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Microbiology, Biotechnology, Biology or a related discipline
You can demonstrate an interest in building a career in Research & Development within an FMCG and/or food manufacturing environment
You are curious, open to learning and actively seek feedback
You are a self-starter who takes ownership, prioritises effectively and adapts to changing priorities
You can influence, listen and build trust with internal and external stakeholders
You are ambitious, challenge the status quo and look for scalable ways to improve the business
You are flexible to work across different sites and functions
You are eligible to work permanently in the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland
Discover Your Future with Kinisla
Kinisla is a vertically integrated dairy, nutritional ingredients and consumer foods business, built on more than 50 years of expertise in milk processing, dairy and nutritional ingredient technology, and product innovation.
Working in close partnership with 2,600 family farms, we produce high-quality, low-carbon-intensity milk for dairy and nutritional ingredient solutions, alongside a strong portfolio of trusted, market-leading consumer products and brands.
With manufacturing operations across Ireland, Northern Ireland and the UK, and a global customer reach, Kinisla is a trusted and forward-looking supplier of high-quality dairy products, ingredients and nutritional solutions. Our four business areas are Agribusiness, Dairy Ingredients, Nutritional Ingredients, and Consumer Foods.
Our purpose is to reimagine dairy for better food and a future worth farming for. Through expertise, innovation and responsible growth, we are helping to shape a more regenerative and climate-conscious future for our dairy.
Rooted in the South-West of Ireland, Kinisla combines deep heritage, global expertise and innovation to create exciting products, partnerships and careers. Our values are Together, Braver, and Further.

Building a sustainable tomorrow. That’s our mission and our promise at BAM. It’s how we engineer vital infrastructure and construct high-quality buildings as one of the largest construction companies in Europe.
We strive to create an environment where everybody feels welcome and valued. We’re on an exciting journey to employ the best talent to join us regardless of social background, race, colour, religion, national or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability or other characteristics.
About The Role
We are recruiting a Site Agent to join our team on a civils project in Cork.
What’s in it for you?
Opportunities! Opportunities to work with a great team on some of Irelands largest, dynamic and most exciting construction, civil and FM projects. Opportunity to develop your skills to the highest industry standards at one of the country's largest construction firms.
We are committed to our employees and offer strong competitive salaries along with great benefits.
8% pension contribution.
Private Health Insurance.
Dental Plan.
26 days annual leave, incremental with years service.
2 Wellbeing days annually.
Paid maternity & paternity leave.
Learning & Development opportunities - internal progression is encouraged and fostered.
Company vehicles (role dependent).
.....and many more great perks.
Making Possible
Design review of submissions for earthworks, pavement, road furniture, markings and finishings to ensure it complies with the contract requirements.
Prepare method statements, inspection and test plans and risk assessments.
Responsible for the technical development of staff members.
Review quality of work on all ongoing works.
Ensure compliance with standards and specifications for pavement design and workmanship.
Supervision of earthworks, subbase, CBGM and asphalt pavement construction.
Monitors work on an ongoing basis to ensure accurate testing.
Review and advise the design team of any modifications needed to the detailed road designs.
Propose cost effective and innovative solutions to the problems in road/pavement, roadworks and finishing works.
Prepare estimates and participate in tender reviews as required.
Manage and price contract variations (continuing variations and improvement works).
Prepare and issue price enquiries.
Prepare scoping documentation, seek suppliers / subcontractors, obtain quotations, undertake the technical evaluation, and make recommendations for the procurement of materials and services.
Communicate with, and attend project progress meetings with the internal site team and clients.
Liaise with the Construction/Project Manager, client and supplier on technical matters as required.
What do you bring to the role?
Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering, or Geotechnical engineering or related Engineering field.
Experience in supervising, coordinating and managing earthworks activities.
Familiarity with specification for highway works and contract document preparation.
Sound knowledge of Microsoft Office suite of software.
Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills.
The ability to lead, manage and proactively participate in project teams.
Hold a valid Drivers Licence.
The application process

jobs.title: Spare Parts Administrator
jobs.desc:
Rockwell Automation is a global technology leader focused on helping the world’s manufacturers be more productive, sustainable, and agile. With more than 28,000 employees who make the world better every day, we know we have something special. Behind our customers - amazing companies that help feed the world, provide life-saving medicine on a global scale, and focus on clean water and green mobility - our people are energized problem solvers that take pride in how the work we do changes the world for the better.
We welcome all makers, forward thinkers, and problem solvers who are looking for a place to do their best work. And if that’s you we would love to have you join us!
Job Description
Are you organized, precise, and passionate about keeping operations running smoothly behind the scenes? Rockwell Automation is hiring a
Spare Parts Administrator
to support critical maintenance, repair, and logistics activities for our customer site in Cork. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a structured environment, enjoys coordinating service tasks, and values precision in documentation and inventory control.
As a
Spare Parts Administrator,
you'll play a vital role in ensuring the availability, accuracy, and flow of spare parts and service-related transactions. You'll collaborate with internal teams, vendors, and customer stakeholders to support maintenance operations and uphold service standards.
You will report directly to the Asset Management Program Manager (AMP) and will be based in Cork Ireland at customer site.
Your Responsibilities
Audit incoming and outgoing shipments for accuracy and quality
Maintain and update inventory records and transaction logs
Process goods receipts and issues in ERP systems
Support daily store operations including stock checks and documentation
Create and manage requests for quotes (RFQs)
Approve and track quotes, orders, and delivery timelines
Archive service documentation and maintain organized records
Generate work orders for equipment repairs and replacements
Coordinate with third-party vendors for parts and service activities
Conduct routine stock counts and maintenance checks
Provide weekly updates and reports to internal and external stakeholders
Ensure compliance with established procedures and reporting standards
The Essentials - You Will Have
Bachelor's degree.
Background in maintenance or logistics.
Familiarity with ERP systems and digital tools for inventory and workflow management.
Attention to detail and organizational skills.
Work collaboratively across departments and communicate clearly.
A mindset with a desire to improve processes and solve issues.
Understanding of how spare parts administration supports broader operational goals.
The Preferred - You Might Also Have
2+ years experience in in industrial manufacturing, MRO planning, or supply chain operations.
Typically requires no previous professional experience.
What We Offer
Our benefits package includes …
Volunteer Paid Time off available after 6 months of employment for eligible employees
Company volunteer and donation matching program – Your volunteer hours or personal cash donations to an eligible charity can be matched with a charitable donation
On-demand digital course library for professional development
Comprehensive mindfulness programs with a premium membership to Calm
Employee Assistance Program
Personalized wellbeing programs through our OnTrack program
and other local benefits!
At Rockwell Automation we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this or other roles.

jobs.title: Sales Advisor - Christmas - Operations - Douglas Village
jobs.desc:
All the details
Join our team this Christmas and help deliver an exceptional experience for our customers during one of the busiest times of the year.
This is a
fixed-term seasonal contract ending on 26 December 2026
, with the possibility of an extension subject to business needs.
Shifts may be scheduled across Monday to Sunday and can include a combination of
core daytime, evening and weekend hours.
Flexibility is essential, as working patterns will vary in line with customer demand and business needs throughout the festive season.
Looking for a role that keeps you moving, gives you variety, and puts you right at the heart of a busy M&S Food store?
We’re looking for an
Operations Customer Assistant
to join our team at
M&S Douglas Village
. This is the role that keeps everything flowing behind the scenes, from deliveries and stock to making sure the shop floor is full, tidy, and ready for our customers.
It’s fast-paced, physical, and hands-on. You’ll be on your feet, moving stock, working deliveries, using digital tools, and supporting the wider store team wherever needed. No two shifts feel the same, so this is perfect for someone who likes being busy, working with purpose, and being part of a team that gets things done.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll help keep the store running smoothly by:
Working deliveries and moving stock quickly and safely & keeping our shelves full, clean, and customer-ready.
Using digital tools to track stock and support availability.
Working across the store when needed, from back of house to shop floor
Supporting your team during busy periods
Staying organised, focused, and one step ahead
Everyone’s Welcome
M&S is ready to push boundaries to lead the retail industry into a greener, speedier, more inspiring digital era. That’s why we’re revolutionising how we work and offering our most exciting opportunities yet. There’s never been a better time to be part of our team. Marks & Spencer aims to be an inclusive organisation, trusted and admired by our colleagues, customers and suppliers. Join us and make an immediate impact.
We are committed to an active Inclusion, Diversity and Equal Opportunities Policy, which starts with our recruitment and selection process, and we are happy to talk flexible working.

jobs.title: Graduate - Asset Management (Infrastructure)
jobs.desc:
See it differently
You see the world through a unique lens and that’s exactly what we need. We embrace how you see things differently – it’s essential for creating a sustainable future.
Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates and students who help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities.
The Opportunity
The Asset Management (Infrastructure) team is part of Management Consulting and helps to deliver and sustain organizational and operational outcomes by supporting clients’ use of technology, primarily in transportation, to achieve their objectives. The team also supports the development of strategies, implementation plans, technology deployments, and performance management. The team supports clients in the management of operations and maintenance contracts relating to transport technology.
As Part Of The Asset Management Team, You Will
Support turning technical recommendations into solutions and project deliverables
Support clients in utilising technology to solve problems and to support transport operations
Undertake analytical research to develop, document and present concepts and design ideas
Review project documentation, applicable codes and standards to assist with preparation of reports, presentations, drawings and/or sketches
Become familiar with technological advances that could provide solutions to client issues
https://www.arup.com/services/intelligent-mobility-systems/
https://www.arup.com/services/asset-management/
Is this role right for you?
For this opportunity, we are seeking the following qualifications, skills and attributes:
An undergraduate or bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in one of the following disciplines:
Civil Engineering
Telecommunications Engineering
Business & Commerce
Project & Programme Management
Transport
Infrastructure
Asset Management
Project Management
We're looking for candidates who can demonstrate some of the following:
An interest in infrastructure asset management and the challenges facing transport and infrastructure owners.
Knowledge of, or enthusiasm for learning about, transport technologies such as:
Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS), Road User Charging; Traffic Signal Design;
Experience producing technical reports, presentations and other project documentation.
An ability to engage effectively with clients, stakeholders and project partners to understand and develop project requirements.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret information and develop practical solutions.
We Are Interested In Graduates Who Can Demonstrate
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
The ability to understand context and consider the broader impact of decisions.
A collaborative approach and ability to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise work, manage competing deadlines and deliver high-quality outputs.
Curiosity, enthusiasm and a willingness to learn and develop professionally.
To Be Considered For a Graduate Opportunity, Your Application Must Include a Copy Of Your Academic Transcript And Meet The Following Criteria
Full working rights in the country of application
No more than 12 months of full-time experience in a comparable role
Recently graduated, or on track to graduate, from your most recent degree, related to your role of choice, before employment starts.
Alongside your degree, we look for the following core attributes;
Changemakers: A passion for sustainable development and creating a better world is key.
Innovative minds: We’re looking for critical thinkers who embrace new ideas and challenge the status quo.
Growth seekers: You have a growth mindset, always eager to learn and explore new ways of working.
Adaptable adventurers: You’re ready to take on any challenge that comes your way.
Closing Date:
12 November 2026
Please note, in the event of high applicant volume, this role may be closed ahead of the advertised closing date. We encourage you to apply early.
Eligibility
We're able to consider candidates who require an employment permit to work in Ireland, where the role and offered salary meet the Irish Government's eligibility criteria (for example, under the Critical Skills or General Employment Permit schemes). All Employment Permits are granted at the discretion of the Deciding Officer with offers contingent to obtaining the correct immigration to work and reside in Ireland."
What we offer you
At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.
Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.
We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling permanent members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
We take an approach to flexible working that supports the diversity and wellbeing of our graduates.
Different people, shared values
Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas - this drives our excellence.
Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas.
We are committed to providing an inclusive recruitment process. Candidates may inform us of any disability, learning difference, or other circumstance that may require reasonable adjustments for interviews or assessments. Any information provided will be used only to make appropriate arrangements and will not be considered in any other aspect of your application or selection process.

A Customer Services Business Partner is required by CareerWise Recruitment to join our North Cork based food production client. This is an exciting opportunity join a well-established business as they go through an expansion phase.
Role
* Lead, motivate and develop the Customer Service team, setting objectives and ensuring high standards of performance and customer satisfaction.
* Oversee the end-to-end order management process, from order receipt and processing through to delivery.
* Manage customer complaints, service incidents and escalations, maintaining strong relationships with key and strategic accounts.
* Monitor and analyse key performance indicators (KPIs), including service levels, OTIF, response times and customer satisfaction (NPS).
* Prepare regular management reports, identify performance trends and implement corrective actions to improve service delivery.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives, standardising processes and optimising CRM, ERP and WMS systems.
* Coordinate closely with Logistics, Transport, Sales and Finance to ensure customer commitments are met and operational issues are resolved.
* Support strategic account management, proactive customer communications, credit notes, collections and commercial documentation.

* Contribute to management meetings, providing insights into customer service performance, operational challenges and improvement opportunities.
Requirements:
* Degree in Business Administration, Logistics, Engineering, International Trade or a related discipline.
* Minimum of 3–5 years' experience in Customer Service, ideally within a logistics, distribution or supply chain environment.
* Proven ability to lead, motivate and develop a team while maintaining high service standards.
* Strong experience in order management, complaint resolution, customer relationship management and cross-functional coordination.
* Advanced Excel skills, including pivot tables, data analysis and reporting.
* Experience using CRM and ERP systems, with SAP knowledge desirable; WMS experience is an advantage.
* Strong understanding of customer service KPIs, including OTIF, service levels, response times and customer satisfaction metrics.
* Experience with Power BI or similar data visualisation and reporting tools.

jobs.title: Control & Protection Engineer
jobs.desc:
Control & Protection Engineer (Cork)
Position Summary
NeoDyne are recruiting a
Control & Protection Engineer
to join our expanding Transmission & Distribution team. The successful candidate will support the design, configuration, and commissioning of protection and control systems for substations, renewable energy projects, and industrial power systems. Prior experience in these areas is highly desirable but not essential as we will provide all training.
The role is offered as a full-time staff position, based at our
Cork Office
, with an excellent Salary and Benefits package. If successful, you will enjoy NeoDyne's "People First" company culture, built on mutual respect, trust, and honesty, where each individual actively contributes as a valued team member.
Company Overview
NeoDyne is a leading engineering company specialising in industrial automation, digital manufacturing, and electrical engineering solutions. We develop high-availability automation and electrical systems for mission-critical industries, including pharmaceutical manufacturing, data centres, and energy infrastructure, ensuring continuous operation and compliance. Our expertise extend across power generation, natural gas transmission, and high-voltage system design, delivering robust solutions that strengthen critical infrastructure.
Within our
Transmission & Distribution
team, we deliver mission-critical design packages that transform the reliability, availability, and efficiency of the energy network, moving it towards a greener, more sustainable future. Department highlights include:
Driving complex design delivery: We design AIS/GIS substations from 20kV to 220kV and contestable build and non-contestable stations in the range of 40 to 550MVA CCGT. Connections include conventional and renewable Power Generation, Peaking, Battery Storage, DS3 and Solar PV plants and large demand loads such as data centres and process plants.
Delivery of high-complexity design frameworks: NeoDyne is a gas network design framework supplier, playing a significant role in providing electrical and instrumentation engineering services for the on-shore Natural Gas Industry and Regulated gas utility sector in Ireland and the UK. Our expertise include Compressor Station, AGI Electrical & Instrumentation design, Fiscal and non-Fiscal metering, and Cathodic Protection.
With a team of 220+ skilled engineers, our expertise spans the entire project lifecycle, from design and implementation to commissioning and operations. From our offices in Ireland, the UK, Romania, and the US, we operate on a global scale, combining technical expertise with local delivery. We support customers across Europe, North America, and Asia, delivering tailored engineering services that drive long-term success.
Key Responsibilities
Design and Engineering
Develop Protection and Control (P&C) designs for HV and MV substations, including protection schemes, control schematics, SLDs, and interlocking diagrams.
Specify and design AC/DC auxiliary systems, control panels, marshalling cabinets, and wiring diagrams.
Prepare Protection Coordination Studies, fault current calculations, and relay grading reports.
Select and configure protection relays and prepare detailed relay setting files.
Design and implement substation automation systems (SAS), RTU/PLC logic, and IEC 61850-based systems.
Create detailed control logic diagrams, signal lists, and communication interfaces for SCADA, RTU, and IED integration.
Testing, Commissioning, and Verification
Develop Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) procedures for control and protection systems.
Carry out relay testing, secondary injection, and end-to-end testing.
Verify correct protection functionality, trip logic, interlocking, and communication protocols.
Provide on-site technical support during commissioning, energisation, and fault-finding phases.
Documentation and Compliance
Produce comprehensive design documentation, wiring schedules, technical specifications, and as-built drawings.
Ensure compliance with EirGrid, ESB Networks, and IEC/EN standards, as well as client-specific design rules.
Support the development and continuous improvement of design templates, engineering standards, and QA processes.
Project Delivery and Collaboration
Reporting to the Lead or Senior Engineering Manager on projects
Providing guidance and training to junior and graduate engineers.
Engage with clients, OEMs, and suppliers to clarify design interfaces, technical requirements, and delivery schedules.
Support proposal development, cost estimation, and technical tender reviews for new projects.
Experience & Skills
Required
Level 8 Degree in Electrical, Energy Engineering, or equivalent
4+ years' experience in a similar electrical or substation design role
Experience in developing Electrical Schematics using EPLAN.
Desired
Knowledge and experience in the Energy sector
Knowledge of Excel for calculations.
Characteristics
We look for candidates who
Work well as part of a team.
Have excellent problem solving and diagnostic skills.
Can complete tasks independently, capable of self-learning.
Can prioritise and coordinate work.
Have excellent customer service, interpersonal, communication and organisational skills.
Can multitask and work well under pressure.
Are a strategic business thinker.
What's on offer?
An opportunity to expand your knowledge beyond control & protection through company training, for example: Earth Grid Design, Reactive Power, Load Flow & Short Circuit Analysis, Substation Layouts Design, HV & MV Equipment Sizing and verification.
Competitive starting salary with year-on-year bonuses and salary increases.
Paid Overtime
PRSA pension with employer contribution
Health Insurance
Income Protection
Life Assurance
Flexible Working
Apply Now

The Naval Service is the State's principal seagoing agency with a general responsibility to meet contingent and actual maritime defence requirements.
We are now recruiting qualified Maintenance Engineers and Technicians to join as Direct Entry Engine Room Artificers (ERAs). In this role, you'll maintain and repair critical onboard systems including propulsion, power generation and auxiliary machinery. Duties include preventative maintenance, fault diagnosis and participation in emergency response operations at sea.

The Naval Engine Room Artificer (ERA) is responsible for maintaining, repairing and ensuring the efficient operation of ship propulsion systems, power generation and auxiliary machinery

ERAs play a vital role in ensuring operational readiness and safety at sea, contributing to the Irish Naval Service’s mission of maritime security and defence.

You will diagnose faults and carry out troubleshooting procedures to ensure continuous operation.

jobs.title: Shipping and Receiving Coordinator 3-Month Contract
jobs.desc:
Who We Are
Transcat is a dynamic, innovative and growing company, recognised as a leading calibration and compliance services provider in North America and beyond. With over 1,000 employees across technical, operational and corporate functions, we deliver on our Trust in Every Measure promise to customers in vital industries, including life sciences, aerospace, defence, energy and utilities. Our employees are at the heart of everything we do, living Our Values every day, the Transcat Way. We are committed to delivering meaningful work that makes a difference for our customers while providing opportunities for our employees to grow and develop their careers.
Transcat In Ireland
Our Irish operation is based in Mitchelstown, Co. Cork, where we provide specialist calibration services to customers across a range of industries. As part of a growing global organisation, our local team plays an important role in delivering reliable, high-quality services while maintaining the collaborative and supportive environment of a smaller operation.
Position Details
Location: Mitchelstown, Co. Cork (fully on-site)
Contract: Full-time, 3-month fixed-term contract
Hours: 39 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Pay: €17.00-€19.00 per hour, depending on experience
Start Date: Immediate
Future Opportunities: Potential for contract extension or longer-term employment, depending on business needs.
Shipping And Receiving Coordinator Role Overview
We are seeking a Shipping and Receiving Coordinator to join our team in Mitchelstown on a three-month fixed-term contract, with an immediate start. This is a hands-on, warehouse-based role combining the physical handling of customer equipment with computer-based processing and administration. Responsibilities include receiving and recording incoming equipment, organising items for calibration, and processing, packaging and dispatching completed equipment back to customers. The role also involves driving a company vehicle to customer sites for equipment collections and deliveries, typically twice a month, during normal working hours. This short-term position will support our operations during a busy period, with the potential for longer-term opportunities depending on business needs.
Duties And Responsibilities
Receiving Equipment: Receive, unpack and inspect incoming customer equipment, checking items against delivery documentation and identifying any discrepancies.
System Processing: Accurately enter and update equipment information in our internal calibration tracking system.
Equipment Organisation: Label, organise and prepare incoming equipment for the calibration team.
Shipping and Dispatch: Prepare calibrated equipment for return to customers, including system processing, checking documentation, packaging and labelling.
Courier Coordination: Arrange shipments and collections with couriers and freight providers, ensuring equipment is dispatched on time.
Customer Collections and Deliveries: Drive a company vehicle to customer sites, typically twice a month, to collect and deliver equipment, including safely loading and unloading items.
Record Keeping: Maintain accurate shipping, receiving and equipment records and communicate any issues or discrepancies to the relevant team members.
Team Collaboration: Work closely with Customer Service and the calibration team to ensure equipment moves efficiently through the service process.
Equipment Handling and Safety: Ensure customer equipment is handled, stored and transported safely in line with company procedures.
Continuous Improvement: Support improvements to shipping, receiving and warehouse processes.
Perform other duties as required.
Experience And Key Competencies
Previous experience in shipping and receiving, warehouse operations, logistics, delivery driving or a similar role is desirable.
A full, valid driving licence is essential, as driving a company vehicle for customer collections and deliveries is a regular requirement of the role.
Comfortable carrying out hands-on warehouse activities, including unpacking, packing, loading and unloading equipment safely.
Good computer skills, including data entry and the ability to learn internal systems.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy when handling equipment and processing information.
Good organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage daily priorities.
Strong communication skills and a professional approach when interacting with customers and colleagues.
Ability to work independently and as part of a small team.
A proactive, reliable and flexible approach to work.
Equal Opportunity And Non-Discrimination
As an equal opportunity employer, we are proud to be a company that embraces the value of bringing diverse, talented, and committed people together. Please don't hesitate to contact the Recruiter assigned to this role should you need any support during our recruitment process.

jobs.desc:
The Naval Service is the State's principal seagoing agency with a general responsibility to meet contingent and actual maritime defence requirements.
We are now recruiting qualified Electrical Engineers to join as Direct Entry Electrical Engineering Officers. This is a leadership and technical role at the heart of Naval operations, with responsibility for managing critical onboard systems and supporting mission success at sea and ashore.
About the Role:
Electrical Engineering Officers (ELOs) are responsible for the design, installation, maintenance and upgrade of complex systems across the fleet, including power generation, navigation, communications, weapons systems, environmental control and IT infrastructure.
During sea postings, you will be a key member of the ship’s engineering department, responsible for electrical, electronic and control systems governing manoeuvrability, defence and intelligence functions.
You will play an active leadership role within the Naval Service, with training at the Naval College to prepare you for both engineering and military responsibilities.
ELOs may serve on ships, ashore, or in overseas assignments.
After a sea rotation, you will take up a shore-based role at the Naval Dockyard, Naval College (NMCI), or Naval Base, managing areas such as project planning, equipment procurement and maintenance operations.
Officers are encouraged to undertake funded Continual Professional Development (CPD) in areas such as Project Management, Engineering Master’s programmes, ATEX Standards, Energy Management, Vibration Analysis and Health & Safety qualifications.

Level 8 (or higher) Honours Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering
Or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Minister for Defence
Applicants must be under 50 years of age on 31 December in the year of application: you will be required to provide proof of your age if you progress to the next stage of the competition.
You must be at least 5ft 2in (157.48cm) in height. You will be measured during the selection process.
No tattoos are to be visible above the collar while serving in the Defence Forces. This will be checked during the selection process and you may not proceed if you have visible tattoos above your collar.
Applicants must meet the work permit eligibility criteria to serve as part of the Defence Forces. i.e. You must have a minimum of 5 years eligibility to stay in Ireland. You will be requested to provide proof of working permit on your application.

Working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, clients, specialist consultants, developers and EPC contractors.

Supporting the wider team in the successful delivery of high voltage and renewable energy infrastructure projects.

5 years' post-qualification experience upwards

A relevant Level 8 minimum third-level degree in Engineering or a related discipline.

Experience in one or more of the following areas: Civil, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, SCADA, HV Transmission, Renewable Energy or Project Management.
Strong professional and technical knowledge within your area of expertise.
Experience working on or supporting the delivery of HV stations, cables, OHL or renewable energy projects, with offshore wind experience highly desirable.
Strong communication, coordination and interpersonal skills.
The ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
Excellent problem-solving skills and a strong attention to detail.

jobs.title: Quality Engineer
jobs.desc:
Quality Engineer required for to join a leading electronics manufacturer. Our products improve reliability, safety and performance in complex applications across a wide range of industries including aerospace, defence and medical devices. Candidates must have experience within an electronics manufacturing environment and knowledge of typical failure modes related to electronic components or circuit card assemblies.
Responsibilities
Support Continuous Improvement of Quality & Quality Systems.
Review of customer requirements, identification and ensuring compliance to quality related requirement.
Review and approval of Engineering Change Requests.
Lead and support AS9145 (APQP) activities like Product Specific Quality Plans, FMEA, Control plans, MSA, First Article Inspection Reports and PPAP.
Lead and support 8D investigations of customer claims, provide reports and communication with customers as required.
Monitoring production quality yields and drive improvements by using Lean and Six Sigma methods – such as 5 Whys, FMEA, 8D to create robust permanent corrective actions.
Manage internal non-conformity reports from identification through to closure.
Report quality performance metrics and improvement progress.
Collaborate with production, engineering and project teams to resolve quality issues.
Provide technical quality support to supplier quality engineering and quality inspectors in incoming inspection.
Provide technical quality support to quality inspectors and quality technicians on the production floor.
• Supports internal and external QMS audits.
Experience:
• Degree in relevant engineering or science discipline.
• Min 3-4 years experience as a quality engineer within an electronics manufacturing environment essential and knowledge of typical failure modes related to e.g. electronic components or circuit card assemblies.
• Six Sigma Green or Black Belt certified.
• Good knowledge of industry standards, such as ISO 9001, EN/AS9100, IPC-WHMA-A-620, IPC-A-610 and J-STD-001 is an advantage.
• Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications.
• Good knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Sampling Plans, Statistics, PFMEA and 8D Problem-Solving.
• Excellent written and oral communication skills with an ability to communicate appropriately across the range of roles from senior management to line operators as well as communicating with external parties.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
