jobs.title: Software Quality Assurance Analyst (12 month FTC)
jobs.desc:
Company Overview
At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.
Department Overview
Innovation is the oxygen of our company, and in 2023, we invested more than US$850 million in research and development (R&D). We’re now opening a new Research & Development Centre in Cork, Ireland focused on designing software for the company’s comprehensive land mobile radio (LMR) portfolio, with plans for expansion across other technologies in the future.
Motorola Solutions’ ecosystem of technologies is centred on safety and security, with LMR representing a foundational core. The company has deployed more than 13,000 LMR networks worldwide, trusted by governments and enterprises for highly secure communications designed to work in the most extreme conditions. Modernised with broadband and advanced data applications, LMR remains at the forefront of providing public safety agencies with the communications they rely on and need.
You’ll be part of our diverse and experienced global team, developing meaningful solutions that support thousands of public safety agencies and enterprises worldwide in solving complex safety and security challenges. Come join our team to work on real-world projects with a real-world impact.
Job Description
We're looking for a self-driven Software Quality Assurance Analyst to take on a vital role in our software development quality assurance process. Your primary responsibilities will include analyzing product specifications and executing targeted test cases to confirm compliance with those specifications. As a manual QA tester, you will be instrumental in identifying and resolving defects, preventing them from reaching our end-users.
The ideal candidate will have a familiarity with hardware, software and a keen eye for detail. You will be expected to demonstrate thoroughness in test execution and a commitment to maintaining the highest standards of software quality.
Responsibilities
Understand product requirements and matching test cases
Setup test environment in preparation for manual test case execution
Execute test cases, analyze results and report all detected issues/defects
Track reported issues/defects and perform root cause analysis to understand the underlying problems
Collaborate with other team members and test managers.
Provide technical know-how, documentation and training to test and other business functions
Basic Requirements
Certificate or Diploma in Computer Science (or a related technical field)
Attention to detail
An analytical mindset and strong problem-solving aptitude
Excellent verbal and written communications skills
The following would be advantageous
Working Knowledge of test management SW (e.g. ALM)
Familiarity with manual and regression testing processes
Familiarity with hardware testing (telecommunications/IT networking products )
Travel Requirements
None
Relocation Provided
None
Position Type
New Grad
Referral Payment Plan
No
Company
Motorola Solutions Ireland Limited
EEO Statement
Motorola Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally-protected characteristic.
We are proud of our people-first and community-focused culture, empowering every Motorolan to be their most authentic self and to do their best work to deliver on the promise of a safer world. If you’d like to join our team but feel that you don’t quite meet all of the preferred skills, we’d still love to hear why you think you’d be a great addition to our team.

jobs.title: Calibration Technician
jobs.desc:
LotusWorks is an Engineering Services provider specializing in managing Commissioning, Construction Services, Calibration, Operations & Maintenance scopes of work within global manufacturing facilities. LotusWorks operates globally across EMEA and North America partnering with the world's leading manufacturers across the Semiconductor, Pharmaceutical & Biologics, Medical Device and Data Center sectors. Our team of Engineering and Technical professionals is immersed in cutting-edge technologies and innovations. LotusWorks is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace, integral to our people-first approach.
As a Calibration Technician, you will report directly to the Site Lead and carry out planned and unplanned calibration activities in line with the calibration schedule prepared by the Lead Calibration Technician. The role will have a strong focus on process calibrations, while also supporting gauging calibrations as required. You will ensure that all Inspection, Measurement and Test Equipment (IMTE) is calibrated safely, on time, and in accordance with site quality requirements, with accurate completion of calibration records and timely escalation of any calibration issues. Safety is a line responsibility, and all personnel are responsible for ensuring that work is conducted safely within their direct or indirect supervision.
Responsibilities
Operations & Maintenance
Complete assigned calibration activities in accordance with the schedule prepared by the Lead Calibration Technician, escalating any risks to completion or equipment availability.
Perform process calibrations including pressure transmitters, transducers, manometers, ovens, furnaces, temperature controllers, freezers, pH and conductivity equipment, cleanrooms, cleanlines, refractometers, ultrasonic baths, packaging equipment and other process instrumentation.
Support gauging calibrations, including calipers, micrometers, pin, plug and thread gauges, drop gauges, overlay and TAPPI charts, CMM calibrations and air gauging systems.
Execute planned and reactive calibration activities in a safe, timely and compliant manner, minimizing disruption to production.
Promptly escalate calibration failures, technical issues and any risks to equipment availability.
Quality
Ensure calibration work orders, as-found/as-left results and associated records are completed accurately and on time within the calibration system and in accordance with site standards.
Follow approved procedures and Equipment Work Instructions (EWIs).
Escalate out-of-tolerance or failed calibrations in accordance with site procedures.
Support discrepancy investigations and ensure required actions are completed.
Complete all required training and maintain audit-ready calibration documentation.
Governance & Relationship Management
Report directly to the Site Lead and work to the operational priorities established through the Lead Calibration Technician.
Escalate schedule, quality, safety and technical issues as required.
Maintain strong working relationships with onsite equipment owners and users to coordinate calibration activities and ensure equipment readiness and access.
Collaborate with Quality, EHS, Engineering, Maintenance, Production and Metrology teams to support compliant calibration execution and troubleshooting.
Provide clear and timely updates on calibration progress, equipment failures, delays and required actions.
Resource Management
Manage assigned daily calibration activities efficiently and complete work within agreed priorities and due dates.
Support other Calibration Technicians and participate in cross-training to improve flexibility and coverage across process and gauging activities.
Maintain and develop technical competence in process instrumentation, calibration standards, troubleshooting and site calibration procedures.
Support Functions
Support the creation, review and continuous improvement of Equipment Work Instructions (EWIs), calibration procedures, Calibration Record Forms (CRFs) and Calibration Data Forms (CDFs), where required.
Adhere to all site Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) requirements and the Life Without (LW) safety culture during all calibration activities.
Identify and support opportunities to improve calibration methods, workflow, equipment reliability, efficiency and compliance.
Any other duties or responsibilities that may be assigned to you in your role.
Skills Required
Practical experience in calibration, metrology, instrumentation or a related technical discipline.
Strong knowledge of process instrumentation and calibration principles.
Experience calibrating pressure, temperature, pH, conductivity and other process instrumentation.
Experience with gauging equipment and dimensional measurement techniques is desirable.
Ability to interpret technical procedures, Equipment Work Instructions (EWIs) and calibration documentation.
Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accurate documentation and data integrity.
Ability to identify, troubleshoot and escalate calibration failures and out-of-tolerance conditions.
Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple calibration activities and priorities.
Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with equipment owners and cross-functional teams.
Commitment to maintaining high standards of quality, safety and compliance.
Willingness to participate in cross-training and continued technical development.
Education / Licenses / Certifications
Minimum of Level 7 Qualification in Calibration/Engineering/Metrology or Process Instrumentation.
Proof of education, licenses, and certifications will be required where applicable
Benefits
VHI Healthcare Cover
Life Assurance
Pension Contribution
Training And Educational Assistance
Annual GP Check-Up
Extra Annual Leave
Healthcare Screening
Recognition Rewards

About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer's favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move. jobs.title: Centre Administrator – Innovation & Industry Engagement
jobs.desc:
Centre Administrator – Innovation & Industry Engagement
Tyndall National Institute is an international leader in semiconductors, photonics and deep-tech research and innovation. As a leading collaborative European research institute, Tyndall is a key actor and hosting partner in the delivery of the ‘Chips for Europe Initiative’ (EU Chips Act).
Tyndall is Ireland’s leading research and innovation organisation and it is the national focal point for excellence in deep-tech research, development and graduate training at the convergence of nanotechnology, microelectronics, photonics, electronics and AI. Tyndall is recognised as an international research leader in semiconductor, chip and digital technologies, particularly as applied to the fields of Information & Communications, Health & Life Sciences, Agritech & Food Security, Energy and Climate Mitigation, emerging fields such as quantum, and novel computing paradigms.
The Institute’s key objective is to see frontier research activities having a significant impact on economic development and societal challenges in Ireland, Europe and beyond. Central to Tyndall’s mission is delivering economic impact through research excellence in partnership with industry and academia. With an annual turnover of more than €50m, the Institute has a community of over 600 researchers, engineers, support staff, postgraduate students, interns and industry researchers-in-residence.
With significant committed Irish government support, Tyndall will grow to be 1,000 people by 2030, with approximately 750 researchers, including 250 PhD students. A new 17,000 m2 research building is under development adjacent to the Cork headquarters and there are developing plans to expand Tyndall’s existing Dublin research labs and to establish other research sites within Ireland.
Tyndall’s expansion is also supported by recent national and EU funding wins for significant (M€10’s) additional research equipment across a range of areas such as semiconductor processing, microscopy, quantum technologies, heterogeneous integration, ultra-high speed optical communications and RF through THz characterisation.
About the Team
The Innovation and Industry Engagement Centre is composed of a team of mostly industry experienced individuals tasked with creating the environment to commercialise Tyndall’s breakthrough innovations to support the growth of Ireland’s semiconductor sector. The team works closely with Tyndall’s researchers to co-develop, and transfer, next generation technologies and to commercialise our platform technologies through spin-out companies. In addition, the Centre hosts the Irish Chips Competence Centre (I-C3), whose role is to support semiconductor start-ups and SMEs with design, access to the EU Pilot Lines, funding and training.
About the Role
You will be an integrated team member in Tyndall’s Innovation & Industry Engagement (I&IE) Centre, supporting the Director and centre staff across a range of administrative activities in the day to day management of the centre. This will involve working closely with the team members to ensure that the centre operates effectively and delivers on its objectives, while also supporting the development and implementation of effective financial, budgetary, quality, client engagement and marketing processes which are key to the institute’s success.
You will also act as the Administrator for hosted I&IE awards, such as the Irish Chips Competence Centre (IC-3). Here you will support the I-C3 team across our partner organisations, MIDAS and Nova UCD in the day to day management of the award and the efficient operation of the centre.
Key Duties & Responsibilities
Efficiently manage all aspects of administration for the centre on a day-to-day basis.
Assist the I&IE Director in the development and management of appropriate administrative structures and procedures
Assist the centre team with KPI reporting
Deal with complex and non-routine queries from staff and external contacts where relevant
Organisation of, and full participation in team meetings with accurate minute taking and coordination of follow up actions
Organisation of industry visits and events and assist with events organised by Tyndall centrally as required
Maintain an awareness of the industry engagement activities of the centre, from client engagement to marketing and out-reach, so as to maximise the effectiveness of the team
Own the administration of the Salesforce CRM and team databases, working with the Director and external service providers to ensure effective implementation and effectiveness of the platform
Manage and assist with any external requirements of the team, including board meetings, conference organisation, external committees and liaison with external clients and stakeholders
Administer all relevant budgetary tasks including purchasing and cost controls for the Centre.
Define and publish financial updates and analysis as may be required by the centre and other functional units in Tyndall
Provide support for incoming visitors and for related seminars/workshops, including any travel arrangements/accommodation and facilities arrangements as required
Provide support for the centre team’s travel arrangements/accommodation and facility needs
Process all procurement for the centre, including related paperwork
Process expenses claims for the centre team and liaise with finance and other operational functions as required.
Liaise with the appropriate Tyndall functions concerning quality, security, safety, maintenance and IT
Provide assistance to the Office of the CEO and other centre administrator positions from time to time as required
Develop and manage an efficient tracking and filing system to allow for immediate access and retrieval of all documentation
Ensure strict confidentiality and discretion on all recruitment/budgetary/financial and staffing matters
Ensure adherence to all relevant Tyndall/UCC procedures and policies as required
Undertake other appropriate duties as assigned from time to time by the I&IE Director
Participate in Education and Public Engagement activities
Ensure compliance with Tyndall’s Quality Management Systems, Health and Safety standards, and other regulations
Essential Criteria
A relevant 3rd level education qualification
5 years’ experience in a similar role at a similar level
Professional, discreet and confidential in approach at all times with an accommodating and efficient manner
Previous experience in a client-facing, sales or marketing operations environment
Previous experience of supporting senior executives in a fast moving environment. e.g. diary management, executive reporting, travel planning et al
Previous experience of client-facing CRM, purchasing management systems, purchase order tracking and related documentation.
Previous financial administration experience in a challenging role
Concise and effective written communication skills
Digital proficiency and the ability to quickly acquire advanced skills with tools such as the Microsoft Office suite of products (i.e. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, etc.), sales and marketing tools (such as Salesforce CRM, Survey Monkey, Eventbrite et al)
Desirable Criteria
Direct, hands-on experience with the Salesforce CRM platform and other sales & marketing tools (as listed above)
Ability to be effective in a collaborative, matrix organisation and influence outcomes from other teams
Excellent organisational, communication and interpersonal skills with an eye for detail. Ability to multi-task and a flexibility and willingness to work additional hours when required
Ability to work on own initiative, both independently and as part of a team.
Strong customer service orientation with the ability to work effectively to achieve tight deadlines
Experience of working within a university environment
What We Offer
Apart from offering a position in a very successful and positive research environment, with a collaborative ethos full of diverse competencies to boost

The Greenkeeper (“G”) position at Hogs Head Golf Club (“HHGC”) is a wonderful opportunity to contribute to one of the top private, resort golf clubs in the world.
HHGC is seeking experienced, dynamic and innovative Greenkeepers to join our exceptional team. As part of our Golf Course & Grounds department, the successful candidate will become part of a dedicated group committed to building, cultivating and delivering an extraordinary experience for our members and guests.

Facility Information
Hogs Head Golf Club was
“Built by Friends, for Friends, for Fun.”
Hogs Head Golf Club has breath-taking vistas including the Finglas River flowing through the course, majestic cliff holes overlooking Ballinskelligs Bay and the seaside charm of Waterville village. Hogs Head Golf Club is an experience unlike any other. It is our personal, sincere and genuine attention to every detail that makes the impossible come to life, creating unique and long-lasting relationships along the way. Designed by legendary golf architect Robert Trent Jones Jr, Hogs Head is a private member's club situated just a mile from Waterville Golf Links on the Ring of Kerry. Named after a marine bearing point on the Ballinskelligs Bay, and completed in 2017, this spectacular layout was voted as the “Best New International Course” by Golf.com. Built on a majestic peninsula outside Waterville Village with stunning sea, mountain, river, and lake views, Hogs Head plays high above the ocean atop dramatic cliffs. It has many classic design features including a nod to Tillinghast's theory on a gentle opening hole, and a Biarritz green (but interestingly found on a par 5). But the most notable inclusion is the 13th - a clifftop par 3, with not one but two infinity greens. Owned and operated by Alvarez & Marsal, Inc., HHGC is not only one of the top club experiences in Ireland, but with a focus on providing an elite, championship golf experience coupled with superior lodging accommodations and service, it is becoming one of the most sought-after clubs in the world.
www.hogsheadgolfclub.com

jobs.desc:
Position summary:
This role will support a wide range of products across multiple surgical specialties, with a primary focus on post-market design support and product performance. Working closely with Quality, Marketing, Operations and Regulatory Affairs, you will investigate customer complaints, field returns and product performance trends to identify opportunities for improvement and support implementation of design changes.
Product Engineering offers a unique opportunity to learn how medical devices perform throughout their entire lifecycle. You will develop deep product knowledge by working on real-world engineering challenges, gaining firsthand experience of how products are designed, manufactured, used by customers and perform in the field. Through investigation of product issues and implementation of improvements, you will help enhance product quality, reliability and customer experience, while contributing valuable insights that influence future product enhancements and next-generation designs.
What you will do:
Support post-market design activities for commercially released medical devices, helping to ensure products continue to meet customer, quality and regulatory requirements.
Investigate customer complaints, field returns and product performance issues using structured problem-solving and root cause analysis techniques.
Partner with Quality, Marketing, Operations and Regulatory Affairs to identify opportunities for product improvements and support implementation of design changes.
Plan and execute engineering testing, verification and validation activities to evaluate product performance and support proposed design improvements.
Support Nonconformance (NC), Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA), and Engineering Change Request (ECR) activities while maintaining compliant engineering documentation.
Develop a deep understanding of Stryker products through real-world engineering challenges, building expertise in product design, manufacturing, customer use and post-market performance while helping drive product improvements and influencing future product designs.
What you will need:
L8 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, or related engineering discipline.
Relevant internship, co-op, university project or research experience is advantageous but not required.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with an interest in understanding how products fail and how they can be improved.
Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams and communicate technical information clearly.
Organised and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple activities and maintain accurate documentation.
A willingness to learn medical device design controls, risk management, verification testing and post-market engineering processes..
Who We Want
Curious problem solvers People who enjoy understanding how products work, investigating problems and identifying root causes.
Eager learners Individuals who seek feedback, continuously develop their technical knowledge and are excited to build expertise in medical device engineering.
Team players Engineers who collaborate effectively across Quality, Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Marketing and Product Engineering.

jobs.title: PhD Positions
jobs.desc:
Three funded PhD positions in iPSC cell therapies.
The iPSC Cell Therapies Lab is recruiting three PhD researchers to work on allogeneic, iPSC-derived immune cell therapies. All three positions are fully funded, covering stipend, tuition and research costs. Candidates may apply to more than one project.
The lab:
Prof. Matsa brings 20 years of experience in iPSC biology, bioprocess development and genome editing across academia and industry, including a postdoctoral fellowship and instructorship at Stanford University School of Medicine and senior leadership roles in cell therapy companies.
The iPSC Cell Therapies Lab, led by Prof. Elena Matsa, works across the School of Biochemistry and Cell Biology at UCC (Cork) and NIBRT (Dublin). Our research goal is to improve the identity, purity, function, yield, reproducibility and cost of iPSC-based immune cell therapies, principally NK, NKT and γδ T cells, and to make them manufacturable at the scale real patient populations need. Current interests span lymphoid lineage development, media formulation, genome editing, scale-up process development, single-cell and in-process analytics, AI-assisted monitoring, and disease-relevant organoid models. Ovarian cancer is our primary clinical indication.
Where you will work:
UCC is a leading Irish university, founded in 1845, with over 20,000 students on a campus overlooking the River Lee in Cork. The School of Biochemistry and Cell Biology holds a strong publication and commercialisation record, with laboratories in the purpose-built Western Gateway Building.
NIBRT, in Dublin, is a global centre of excellence for biopharmaceutical manufacturing research and training. Its facility houses a fully operational pilot plant alongside advanced therapeutics research laboratories, extended in 2023 to grow cell and gene therapy capacity. All three students will split their time between the two sites, gaining academic research training at UCC and industrial bioprocessing experience at NIBRT.
The three projects
Project 1,
Genome engineering, UCC (Y1–2), NIBRT (Y3–4)
You will build a genome engineering toolkit for screening iPSC differentiation at scale: identifying genomic safe harbour loci, knocking in donor DNA by CRISPR/Cas9 ribonucleoprotein delivery, characterising monoclonal lines, and inserting large DNA barcode libraries. You will then apply it to optimise and scale a differentiation process in parallel bioreactor platforms. Skills: construct design and molecular cloning, CRISPR genome editing, single-cell cloning, karyotype and off-target analysis, bioreactor operation.
Project 2,
Immune cell biology, UCC (Y1), NIBRT (Y2–4)
You will develop a differentiation route from iPSC to mature immune effector cells, then determine how well they kill tumour cells and how the tumour microenvironment blunts them, through co-culture with cancer cells, macrophages and fibroblasts, and design strategies to make them more potent. Skills: advanced stem cell culture, multiparameter flow cytometry, cytotoxicity and serial-killing assays, cytokine profiling, live-cell imaging, single-cell transcriptomics.
Project 3,
Immunometabolism and imaging, UCC, with periods at partner institutes (Y1-3.5)
You will define the metabolic programme of each developmental intermediate between iPSC and mature NK cell, and use targeted metabolic interventions to steer differentiation towards a more mature, more potent product. In parallel you will work with photonics engineers at Tyndall National Institute to characterise metabolic states using FLIM technology integrated in a benchtop label-free imaging sensor. Skills: flow cytometric staging and cell sorting, immunometabolic assays, autofluorescence and fluorescence lifetime imaging, image-based analytics, NK cytotoxicity assays.
What we are looking for
•
A primary degree (honours bachelor's or master's) in biochemistry, biomedical science, immunology, biotechnology, bioengineering, biophysics or a related discipline.
•      At least one year of hands-on mammalian cell culture experience, including aseptic technique. Experience with stem cells or primary immune cells is an advantage.
•      Relevant technical experience for your chosen project — molecular cloning or genome editing (Project 1), flow cytometry and functional immune assays (Projects 2 and 3), quantitative microscopy or scripting for data analysis (Project 3).
•      Critical thinking and sound experimental design, with the independence to shape your own project and the judgement to know when to ask.
•      Clear written and spoken English, and the ability to present work to scientists from other disciplines.
•      Good organisation, documentation practice and time management across two sites, and willingness to work occasional weekends when cultures require it.
•      A real interest in cell therapy and its translation, evidenced by prior projects, placements, publications or professional experience.
What you will get
•
Regular one-to-one supervision, a supervisory team spanning both institutions, and annual progress review in line with UCC policy for research students.
•      Access to state-of-the-art instrumentation at UCC core facilities and NIBRT, including automated bioreactor systems, single-cell analytics and advanced imaging platforms.
•      Training in GMP-aligned documentation and bioprocessing alongside academic research skills — a combination that opens both academic and industry careers.
•      Support to publish, present at international conferences and protect intellectual property, and opportunities to co-supervise undergraduate and master's students.
How to apply
Send a motivation letter and curriculum vitae to Prof. Elena Matsa at
ematsa@ucc.ie
, stating which project or projects you are applying for. Informal enquiries welcome at the same address. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the positions are filled.

jobs.desc:
Senior Quantity Surveyor – Structural Steel
📍
Ireland – Southern Ireland Projects
💼
Permanent | Full Time
Steel projects can move quickly.
Drawings change. Site conditions develop. Additional work appears. Subcontractors need managing and clients need paying.
The difference between a project that simply gets delivered and one that delivers commercially comes down to what happens between those moments.
That's where you come in.
As Senior Quantity Surveyor, you'll take ownership of the commercial side of structural steel projects, working closely with project, site and fabrication teams from the initial take-off through to final account.
The Role
You'll be involved across the full commercial lifecycle of your projects.
You'll review drawings, complete take-offs for structural steel, decking and cladding, identify changes from the original tender and make sure those changes are captured commercially.
You'll manage subcontractor procurement and accounts, prepare interim payment applications, negotiate variations and claims, and keep pressure on outstanding client payments.
You'll also spend time on site, seeing the work first-hand and understanding exactly what is happening before making commercial decisions.
From cost planning through to completion, you'll be responsible for making sure the numbers reflect the work being delivered.
What You'll Bring
7+ years' Quantity Surveying experience
Strong background in structural steel or similar specialist construction
Good understanding of contracts and commercial project management
Experience managing variations, claims, procurement and final accounts
Ability to read construction drawings and complete accurate take-offs
Strong negotiation and communication skills
Confident working independently while remaining closely connected to the wider project team
Good knowledge of Excel, Word, Outlook and project management systems
Degree or relevant qualification in Quantity Surveying or a related discipline
Experience within the Irish steelwork market is advantageous, but not essential
Why This Role?
This isn't a QS position where your involvement ends when the numbers go into a spreadsheet.
You'll be close to the projects, visiting sites, working with project teams, dealing directly with clients and subcontractors, and seeing the steel you're commercially responsible for being delivered.
You'll have the opportunity to take real ownership of projects within a specialist structural steel environment, with plenty of scope to use your commercial experience rather than simply administer someone else's processes.
If you're an experienced Quantity Surveyor who understands that you can't properly manage the commercial side of steel without understanding what's happening on site, this could be worth a conversation.
Apply now or get in touch for a confidential discussion.

jobs.title: UX Product Designer
jobs.desc:
Who is Forcepoint?
Forcepoint simplifies security for global businesses and governments. Forcepoint’s all-in-one, truly cloud-native platform makes it easy to adopt Zero Trust and prevent the theft or loss of sensitive data and intellectual property no matter where people are working. 20+ years in business. 2.7k employees. 150 countries. 11k+ customers. 300+ patents. If our mission excites you, you’re in the right place; we want you to bring your own energy to help us create a safer world. All we’re missing is you!
We're looking for a
UX
Product Designer
to lead a comprehensive modernization of the DSPM (Data Security Posture Management) platform's look and feel. Your mission: transform DSPM from functionally sound to visually modern, high-tech, minimalistic, and polished — while maintaining crystal-clear information architecture and usability standards. This is a hands-on design role where you'll directly shape how security teams visualize and understand complex data, while also establishing design standards that prevent usability drift.
You'll be the bridge between design strategy and implementation — working closely with frontend engineers to ship modern, high-fidelity designs while ensuring every feature released maintains usability integrity.
Main Responsibilities
Collaborate and own. Work alongside UX design lead, product owners and engineering. Define UX requirements early, stay in the build through QA and release, and make engineering-aware design decisions.
Establish a modern visual language, interaction patterns for data-heavy interfaces and a coherent design system (tokens, components, patterns) that guides all future work and ensures consistency.
Lead a comprehensive redesign of DSPM's analytics components (charts, tables, filters, data cards, gauges, etc.). Create information architectures and visual hierarchies that make dense datasets scannable and actionable
Conduct regular UX reviews using established usability principles (e.g., Nielsen's heuristics), document deviations and create prioritized initiatives to address them
Design complex, multi-step user workflows that handle security operations (threat detection, policy enforcement, risk assessment). Leverage actively modern AI-assisted design tools to accelerate ideation and rapid prototyping, focusing craft on solving the highest-impact user tests.
Partner closely with frontend engineers on a component-first implementation approach. Treat frontend engineers as your primary collaborator (not as a handoff point)
Create design specs (Figma prototypes, interaction documentation) that guide implementation and provide rapid iteration feedback during development to keep quality high
Ensure design quality at release through comprehensive audits and design sign-off
Core Requirements
5+ years designing enterprise software products (desktop interfaces)
Strong portfolio showing:
Data visualization UI (dashboards, charts, tables, complex workflows)
Component/pattern libraries you've designed or led
Visual design quality — modern, refined, user-focused
Figma proficiency (your primary design tool)
Design system or component library experience (you've owned or significantly contributed)
Excellent visual design skills and knowledge of user-centered design principles.
Usability heuristics mindset: you evaluate designs against established principles, not just gut feel
Collaborative mindset: you thrive in partnership with engineers and product, not in isolation
Strongly Preferred
Enterprise security/B2B product experience
Familiarity with AI design tools or willingness to learn
Experience designing for power users (not consumer-focused, but technical audiences)
Deep product mindset: you understand how products work end-to-end; you've shipped across multiple areas; you think about systems, not just screens
How You Work
Attention to Detail: You have a meticulous eye for visual and interaction details while crafting high-quality, user-friendly experiences.
Master of trade-offs: You can break large features into thoughtful chunks, propose multiple design solutions, and find smart compromises between design vision, implementation timeline, and resource constraints. You speak the language of feasibility without compromising on quality.
Product deep-diver: You don't design in a vacuum. You invest time understanding how DSPM works—the security workflows, user mental models, the competitive landscape, and why design decisions matter. You ask why before designing.
Proactive problem-spotter: You don't wait to be told what to design; you spot gaps and propose solutions grounded in user needs and design principles.
Clear communicator: You explain why, not just show what. Your decisions are defensible; you can articulate the reasoning to engineers, product, and stakeholders.
Humble iterator: You seek feedback early and often — from users, from engineers, from product. You iterate based on reality, not assumptions.
Shipping-focused: Perfect designs that never ship don't help users. You care about getting work into the world and learning from real use.
Don’t meet every single qualification? Studies show people are hesitant to apply if they don’t meet all requirements listed in a job posting. Forcepoint is focused on building an inclusive and diverse workplace – so if there is something slightly different about your previous experience, but it otherwise aligns and you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply. jobs.title: DSP Engineer (Digital Signal Processing)
jobs.desc:
About MBRYONICS
MBRYONICS is at the forefront of free space optical communications. Our product portfolio covers a wide range of emerging technologies from photonic integrated circuits to advanced optical systems and embedded software solutions. Our optical communications systems are integrated and deployed in satellite communications systems. The work is exciting and challenging and is at the forefront of the technology domains. As part of our expansion, we are currently looking for a suitably motivated -
DSP Engineer
- to join our group.
As a Digital Signal Processing (DSP) Engineer at MBRYONICS, you'll be a key player on our engineering team, translating advanced communication theory into reality for our cutting-edge optical communication systems. This role is ideally suited for a fresh PhD graduate looking to transition deep academic expertise into high-impact, space-bound hardware. You will dive into algorithm design, system modeling, and cross-functional hardware integration in a fast-paced, high-tech setting.
What you'll do
Algorithm Development: Design and simulate advanced Digital Signal Processing (DSP) and Forward Error Correction (FEC) algorithms in both floating-point and fixed-point precision to optimize link performance, enhance functionality, and minimize power consumption.
Hardware Co-Design: Collaborate closely with the FPGA engineering team to provide clear fixed-point models and specifications, ensuring a smooth transition of your DSP algorithms into RTL implementation.
System Modeling: Develop comprehensive end-to-end models of analog RF and optical components (including lasers, modulators, photodetectors, and amplifiers) to accurately evaluate and predict system performance under real-world conditions.
Cross-Functional Integration: Partner with optical testing and firmware teams to create robust, automated algorithms for transceiver calibration, beam alignment, and run-time optimization in dynamic space environments.
Validation & Testing: Conduct system-level validation of your models against actual hardware performance, utilizing lab data to refine and iterate your designs.
Documentation: Document your algorithm architectures, simulation results, and fixed-point specifications to support the wider engineering lifecycle.
Who you are
Education: This role would be ideally suited to a Post Doctorate (or nearing completion) with a PHD in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Telecommunications, Physics, or a highly related field with a research focus on DSP or digital communications. We would also welcome applications from candidates with experience in industry rather than academia.
Simulation Mastery: Extensive hands-on experience using MATLAB and Simulink for complex modeling, system simulation, and algorithm development.
Theoretical Grounding: A deep, foundational understanding of digital communication theory, signal modulation, noise modeling, and error-correction techniques.
Fixed-Point Familiarity: Experience converting floating-point algorithms into optimized, bit-true fixed-point models suitable for FPGA or ASIC implementation (academic or project-based experience is highly valued).
Coding Skills: Proficiency in C/C++ or Python for scripting, data analysis, or rapid prototyping is a strong plus.
Problem-Solving Mindset: Strong analytical and mathematical skills, with the academic rigor required to tackle open-ended, complex engineering challenges.
Soft Skills & Passion: Excellent technical communication skills, a collaborative mindset eager to work across disciplines, and a genuine interest in space technology and free space optics.
What's In It For You
Career Growth:
Contribute to a world-class space-age communication program while developing your leadership skills in a state-of-the-art manufacturing environment
Collaboration:
Work with talented professionals across disciplines to drive impactful solutions
Innovation:
Be part of a team pioneering advancements in manufacturing engineering for cutting-edge FSO systems
Work-Life Balance:
Enjoy flexible work schedules and a comprehensive benefits package
If you're ready to take your career to new heights and drive the future of space-age communication, apply now and join the MBRYONICS team as our
D
SP Engineer

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer

The Opportunity
THE OPPORTUNITY
At Stantec Ireland, you’ll join a growing Energy team at the forefront of a transforming transmission and distribution sector. With rising demand and ambitious decarbonisation targets across Ireland , this is an opportunity to contribute to critical infrastructure shaping the energy transition.
As an Electrical Engineer specialising in HV cable design, you’ll work on a diverse range of projects including HVDC interconnectors, offshore and onshore wind, substations, and grid connections—supporting initiatives aligned with EirGrid ’s network development.
You’ll collaborate within a multidisciplinary team across all project stages, from FEED to delivery, contributing technical expertise while developing your career in a supportive, innovation-driven environment.
About The Role
You will take on a key role within our growing Energy team, supporting the design and delivery of high-voltage cable systems across a range of major infrastructure and renewable energy projects throughout Ireland .
Working as part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment, you will contribute to projects spanning HVDC interconnectors, offshore and onshore wind farms, substations, and grid connection schemes. Your responsibilities will include supporting and leading design activities across all project phases—from feasibility and FEED through to detailed design and delivery—ensuring high-quality, efficient, and innovative engineering solutions.
You will work closely with internal teams and external stakeholders, including key clients such as EirGrid , helping to address complex technical challenges and deliver infrastructure that underpins Ireland’s transition to a more sustainable energy future.
This role offers the opportunity to apply your technical expertise, mentor junior engineers, and play an active part in shaping impactful projects, while continuing to develop your career within a supportive and forward-looking organisation.
YOUR IMPACT
In this role, you will help deliver safe, reliable and sustainable water infrastructure for communities across Ireland. Through your expertise in process design, you will develop effective treatment solutions that improve water quality and support resilient systems for the future.
You will assist in the mentorship and training of junior staff throughout there early career stages with Stantec.
Working closely with multidisciplinary teams and clients, you will contribute to innovative, practical solutions across the full project lifecycle. Your work will help ensure designs are efficient, compliant and deliver long-term value while supporting the collaborative culture that defines our team at Stantec.
About You
You are a proactive and technically capable Electrical Engineer with a strong understanding of the electricity transmission and distribution sector.
You will ideally hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering (or a related field) from an accredited institution, with membership of Institution of Civil Engineers (EI) is preferred. You bring experience in civil substation engineering and a broad awareness of HV civil engineering projects.
You have hands-on experience in the design of transmission and distribution systems across all stages (Concept, FEED, and Detail Design), applying international standards for utility clients. You can coordinate effectively across disciplines, resolving design issues and ensuring practical, innovative solutions.
Your Technical Skills Include
Cable installation design, including routing layouts, trench/trenchless sections, bonding and phasing, pulling, termination, and jointing arrangements.
Proficiency with CYMCAP software for cable sizing calculations to international standards.
Strong computer literacy in MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook) and design tools such as AutoCAD or MicroStation.
You are adaptable and capable of managing challenging workloads under changing priorities, delivering high-quality results in a dynamic environment.
WHY JOIN US
We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025.
We do what is right: Industry leading training and development as well as paid for professional subscriptions. A professional progression plan, supporting you to become chartered.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment to assist with the growth of your career.
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard!
About Stantec
Whether you’re starting out on your engineering career or are looking for a fresh challenge, Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, is a great career move.
Based in Dublin, Galway, Castlebar and Cork, we are actively recruiting for team players with experience in any of the following areas – water and wastewater treatment process and network design, integrated network management, structural design, site development, road and bridge engineering, project management and administration.
You’ll be working for a dynamic company with an excellent reputation in the industry.
Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, offers a great working environment amongst friendly professionals with an emphasis on teamwork. It’s a company where your ideas and opinions will be valued and your efforts recognised and rewarded.
We have been awarded the silver Investors in Diversity accreditation by the Irish Centre for Diversity for our commitment to quality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) in the workplace.

jobs.title: Sr. Associate, Sourcing and Procurement
jobs.desc:
Who We Are
BioMarin is a leading rare disease biotechnology company focused on genetically defined conditions.
Guided by our purpose to develop medicines that make a profound impact on people’s lives, our global teams have delivered a portfolio of therapies since our founding in 1997. Our revolutionary treatments for conditions like achondroplasia (the most common form of dwarfism), PKU (phenylketonuria), CLN2, a form of Batten disease, and a number of forms of MPS (mucopolysaccharidosis) offer new possibilities for patients and families who previously had few, if any, available options. More recently, with the close of the Amicus acquisition, our portfolio has expanded to include therapies for Fabry disease and Pompe disease, expanding our ability to reach more people living with rare genetic conditions.
Our success comes from our unwavering commitment to excellence, our deep understanding of patient needs, our scientific expertise, and our world-class manufacturing capabilities. At the heart of BioMarin is a dedicated team of the brightest minds in the industry working together to deliver innovative therapies to patients and families around the world.
About Corporate Groups
It takes a village, and at BioMarin, our general and admin teams are the village behind our success. From the IT experts who manage our technology to the human resources professionals who hire the people who make it all possible, these teams support our organization and span all areas of operations.
Our Culture
Our desire to make a positive impact on our patients extends to our employees and BioMarin is committed to fostering an inclusive environment where every person feels seen, valued, and heard – so employees can thrive in all areas of their lives, in and outside of work. We seek to provide an open, flexible, and friendly work environment to empower people and to provide them with the ability to develop their long-term careers. Ultimately, we want to be an organization where people enjoy coming to work and take pride in our efforts to help patients.
Title: Sr. Associate, Sourcing and Procurement
Location: Shanbally, Ringaskiddy, County Cork
Workstyle: Hybrid
12 month contract
Global Sourcing and Procurement
The Global Sourcing and Procurement (GSP) organization is accountable for driving and delivering Procurement value to support stakeholders’ and organizational strategic objectives. The GSP function delivers value to BioMarin by leading transformation change and implementing industry-leading category strategies that directly support the corporate strategy. The GSP organization leverages market intelligence, subject matter expertise, and business insights in the procurement of goods and services and management of BioMarin’s growing third-party spend of $1B+. Through collaboration with our external suppliers and internal business partners, GSP helps bring innovative new medicines to patients.
Role Purpose
The
Sr. Associate, Sourcing and Procurement
is an individual contributor role reporting to the Sr. Category Manager, Logistics and Distribution, within BioMarin’s Global Sourcing and Procurement (GSP) organization. This position provides hands-on support across the end-to-end source-to-pay lifecycle – sourcing events, contracting, purchase order management, supplier onboarding, and spend analytics – for the Logistics and Distribution category, including 3PL/warehousing, freight forwarding, courier, cold chain packaging, and temperature monitoring services.
The role partners with the Sr. Category Manager and stakeholders to execute day-to-day sourcing and procurement activities, while building the category management fundamentals, systems expertise, and business acumen needed to progress into a Category Manager role.
Scope & Responsibilities
Sourcing Execution:
Execute sourcing events (RFI/RFQ/RFP) for goods and services within the category, including preparing RFx documents, managing supplier communications, consolidating responses, and building bid comparison and scoring analyses.
Support lane-based freight and courier rate requests, building rate comparisons and cost-to-serve analyses across modes (air, ocean, road) and regions.
Support the Sr. Category Manager in supplier evaluation, selection, and award recommendations, documenting outcomes in line with the Global Sourcing and Procurement Policy.
Manage the sourcing intake queue for lower-complexity requests, independently leading tactical sourcing events and escalating strategic or high-risk requests as appropriate.
Stakeholder Support:
Serve as a responsive point of contact for internal requesters across Global Supply Chain, Distribution, Quality, Trade Compliance, and Clinical Supply, guiding them through procurement processes and policy requirements.
Gather and clarify stakeholder requirements, scope, timelines, and budget to enable efficient sourcing and contracting.
Support resolution of supplier issues related to delivery, invoicing, or service performance, coordinating actions across functions and escalating as needed.
Contracting & Purchase Order Management:
Draft and route standard agreements (e.g., NDAs/CDAs, MSAs, SOWs, change orders, amendments) using approved templates, in partnership with Legal and the Sr. Category Manager.
Support commercial negotiations on pricing and terms for assigned spend under the guidance of the Sr. Category Manager.
Review purchase requisitions for policy compliance, correct commodity coding, and alignment to contract value; support PO creation, change orders, and closure.
Maintain contract repository records, track renewal and expiration dates, and initiate renewal activities ahead of deadlines.
Supplier Management:
Coordinate supplier onboarding and setup, including due diligence, risk assessments, and required documentation.
Track logistics supplier KPIs/SLAs (e.g., on-time delivery, temperature excursions, damage/loss, invoice accuracy), rebates, and value realization, and prepare materials for supplier business reviews.
Monitor supplier risk indicators and flag concerns to the Sr. Category Manager.
Spend Analytics & Reporting:
Extract, cleanse, and analyze spend data from Ariba, SAP, and related systems to identify savings, consolidation, and compliance opportunities.
Build and maintain dashboards and reports (e.g., Power BI, Excel) for spend, savings, contract coverage, and pipeline tracking.
Track and document hard and soft savings in alignment with GSP savings methodology and Finance requirements.
Support market research and benchmarking to inform category strategies.
Systems, Compliance & Continuous Improvement:
Maintain high data integrity across procurement and quality systems (Ariba, SAP, GEP Smart, Veeva, Power BI, SharePoint Lists, etc.).
Support trade compliance reviews of international shipments, including Incoterms, duties, and tariff validation, in partnership with Global Trade Compliance.
Support policy compliance, audit requests, and execution of GSP business processes.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that simplify procurement processes, tools, and requester experience.
Qualifications
Required:
Bachelor’s degree (NFQ Level 7/8 or equivalent) in supply chain, business, finance, engineering, life sciences, or related discipline.
2–4 years of experience in procurement, sourcing, supply chain, or related roles.
Working knowledge of the source-to-pay process, including sourcing, contracting, purchase orders, and supplier management.
Strong analytical skills with advanced Excel proficiency; experience working with large data sets.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple requests and priorities with attention to detail.
Clear written and verbal communication skills and a customer-service mindset with internal stakeholders.
Ability to work effectively in cross-functional and global team environments, including collaboration with US-based colleagues across time zones.
Preferred:
Experience in biotech, pharmaceutical, medical

jobs.desc:
Your mission
Assure compliance with regulatory requirements related to clinical operations
Responsible for securing and developing all records, equipment and programmes related to occupational health services
Annual review of all Occupational Health Policies and Procedures in line with legislation, business changes and audit requirements.
Completion of pre-employment medicals, interpretation of results and compiling reports
Carry out risk assessments across the organization as required.

Liaising with OHPs, GPs, Physiotherapists and Consultants in managing cases.

Registered General Nurse with a valid NMBI registration
Competency in Audiometry, Spirometry, Vision screening, phlebotomy, VDU ergonomics & administration of vaccines.
Excellent communication skills with strong interpersonal, empathy and listening skills.

Medmark is a leading national provider of occupational health. jobs.title: Marketing Intern, EMEA
jobs.desc:
Description
Keeper Security is seeking a dynamic and motivated Marketing Intern to support the EMEA Growth Marketing team. This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in B2B marketing, demand generation, and marketing operations within the cybersecurity industry. They will play an active role in supporting marketing campaigns, lead generation initiatives, and digital marketing activities across the EMEA region. This is a 100% remote internship from select locations, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for those candidates based in the Cork City area.
Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organisations, globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and is sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and gain valuable skills assisting our marketing department in our promotional efforts.
About Keeper
Keeper Security is a leading cybersecurity software company that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in more than 150 countries. Keeper delivers a powerful zero-trust and zero-knowledge solution built to meet the stringent requirements of public sector IT environments. Its flagship offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects users, devices and critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized in the Gartner® Magic QuadrantTM for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper combines robust compliance with unmatched visibility and control. With industry-leading certifications, Keeper provides the security assurance public sector organizations require. Learn why agencies trust Keeper to defend against today’s sophisticated adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com.
About The Role
The Marketing Intern will report to the Senior Marketing Manager, EMEA and will be responsible for supporting the EMEA Growth Marketing team on daily tasks and projects. This is a 3-month internship with the possibility of extension, contingent on company needs and performance.
This is a paid internship designed to offer professional experience in marketing and demand generation.
Please note that we do not offer school credit for this internship.
Responsibilities
Assist the EMEA team execute and manage marketing/demand generation activities, including field events, email campaigns, display ads, webinars, social media initiatives and content development that drive new business.
Help with setting up digital marketing campaigns in LinkedIn, XING, Reddit, Demandbase, HubSpot.
Provide general marketing support to the team for the coordination of campaigns and projects.
Collaborate with other Keeper marketing teams to implement international programs like PPC, SEO, PR and more.
Assist with monitoring campaign performance and reporting.
Requirements
Current enrollment in or recent completion of a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (Undergraduate or Postgraduate degree) in Marketing, Communications, Business or a related field preferred.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.
Detail-oriented with a commitment to accuracy and quality in all deliverables.
Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and take initiative on assigned tasks.
Basic working knowledge of Google (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive) and Microsoft Office products.

Familiarity with marketing automation platforms and CRM systems would be a distinct advantage (e.g. HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot, Salesforce).
Previous marketing internship or relevant work experience.

This is a full-time role based on-site in the heart of Cork city.

Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. We are ideally looking for a full-time permanent surgeon; however, we are open to discussing flexible or part-time arrangements for the right candidate.
With a preferred start date from November 2026 onwards (flexible), this position offers exceptional clinical freedom, excellent facilities and genuine scope to shape the role around your interests and professional ambitions.
Located just a short distance from Cork city centre, Sunbeam offers an excellent base for enjoying everything the city and wider county have to offer. Cork combines a vibrant food, culture and social scene with easy access to some of Ireland’s most beautiful coastline, beaches and countryside. With Cork Airport nearby and excellent transport links, it’s a fantastic place to expand your career while enjoying a great quality of life outside of work.

Sunbeam Veterinary Group is a 100% small animal veterinary group with practices located across Cork, including Blackpool, Cobh, Passage West and Kinsale Road. Our referral centre, based at Northpoint Business Park on Cork's northside, provides advanced surgical, diagnostic and emergency services to patients throughout the region.
We operate a busy referral hospital with 24/7 emergency and critical care support, providing around-the-clock veterinary cover. Our clinical team consists of approximately nine veterinary surgeons, fifteen qualified veterinary nurses, hydrotherapy specialists and a dedicated support team. We also benefit from multiple certificate holders and experienced clinicians across a range of disciplines, creating a highly collaborative and supportive environment.

Hospitalisation and intensive care facilities

You will take responsibility for a busy and varied surgical caseload involving both soft tissue and orthopaedic procedures, managing cases from initial assessment through to surgery and follow-up care. You will work alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team, with access to advanced imaging, rehabilitation services and emergency support.
We are looking for someone who is confident handling referral cases independently and who is excited by the opportunity to further develop and grow surgical services within the practice. There is significant flexibility within this role, allowing the successful candidate to shape the caseload around their individual interests and expertise.
Experience or a strong interest in laparoscopic and endoscopic procedures would be highly advantageous as we continue to develop these services.

jobs.title: Civil Engineer T&D
jobs.desc:

Support the delivery of civil infrastructure for renewable energy projects and electricity networks.
Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach have set us apart for over 75 years, guiding how we shape a better world. We have been present in Ireland since 1946 and we have a team of more than 950 engineers, consultants, and qualified technical personnel. We work for clients from the public and private sectors, providing creative and sustainable solutions based on the efficient use of resources.
Our Energy team in Ireland delivers high‑value technical, design and advisory services across a diverse portfolio of energy and infrastructure projects, supporting the development of a resilient and low‑carbon electricity system. Our work spans electricity transmission and distribution infrastructure, renewable energy integration and grid reinforcement, including civil engineering design to support renewable energy infrastructure, including offshore wind and electricity networks, across Ireland and the wider Arup regions.
The Opportunity
This is an opportunity to join our Energy Infrastructure team and contribute to the delivery of electricity Transmission & Distribution (T&D) projects. The role will involve supporting the civil design and delivery of substations, cable routes and associated infrastructure, providing civil engineering design to support renewable energy infrastructure, including offshore & onshore wind, BESS, Solar and electricity networks. Working as part of multi‑disciplinary project teams from early feasibility and route optioneering through to detailed design and delivery. The successful candidate will work within a well‑established and experienced group, benefiting from strong technical support and exposure to a broad range of civil engineering activities associated with T&D and renewable energy projects. This is a permanent position within the Energy team.
As a Civil Infrastructure Engineer At Arup, You Will
Deliver elements of civil infrastructure design for electricity transmission and distribution projects.
Contribute to the development of underground cable routing, corridor studies and alignment design.
Support the civil design of substations, including site layout design, earthworks, drainage, access arrangements, hardstandings and structural interfaces.
Support civil engineering design for renewable energy electrical infrastructure, including grid connections and onshore works associated with offshore wind projects.
Understand the appointed design scope, identify associated deliverables and define the workflow required to complete assigned elements of work.
Work within a multi‑disciplinary design team, coordinating with electrical, mechanical, environmental and planning specialists to deliver integrated design solutions.
Produce civil design outputs including drawings, reports, specifications and design calculations.
Support delivery of assigned work packages to agreed programme, quality and budget targets.
Plan and manage assigned workload, ensuring appropriate quality assurance and coordination within the design team.
Ensure all designs are completed in accordance with relevant standards, specifications, safety requirements and client procedures.
Does this role inspire you?
We are looking for a proactive engineer with a strong interest in civil infrastructure delivery within the electricity and renewable energy sectors.
The Ideal Candidate Will Have
A relevant third‑level Degree (Level 8 or higher) in Civil Engineering (or a related discipline).
Circa 3–5 years’ post‑qualification experience, primarily in civil design, gained within a consultancy or comparable engineering environment.
Membership of a relevant professional body.
Experience in civil infrastructure design, ideally related to electricity transmission and/or distribution, grid connections or comparable linear infrastructure schemes.
Experience working with/interfacing with Transmission System Operators (TSOs) and/or Distribution Network Operators (DNOs), including familiarity with their standards, specifications and approval processes, would be an advantage.
Experience or exposure to underground utilities and cable infrastructure, including trenching, ducting, protection systems and reinstatement.
Experience in site development and layout design, including earthworks, drainage, access roads and hardstandings.
Familiarity with industry software such as Civil 3D, AutoCAD and/or Revit.
Experience working within multi‑disciplinary design teams and coordinated BIM environments.
Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills.
Good communication skills, with the ability to work effectively within a team environment.
How to apply for this vacancy?
To apply for this vacancy, register your updated CV and a cover letter in English.
Why Arup?
At Arup, we offer a rewarding career with a global company committed to a better future. Our unique trust ownership structure allows us to prioritize meaningful work and invest in our people. We also offer a unique profit share program, allowing our members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
Benefits That Work For You
Professional Growth & Development: Benefit from continuous learning opportunities, training programs, and mentorship to enhance your skills and advance your career at Arup.
Global Opportunities: Collaborate with colleagues worldwide and explore potential short-term or long-term assignments at other Arup offices and project locations.
Financial Well-being & Ownership: Receive a competitive salary and benefits package and share in Arup's success through our global profit-sharing programme.
Work-Life Balance: We offer a hybrid working model and flexible working arrangements to support work-life balance.
Well-being and Culture: Access to a range of well-being programs, including sports subsidies, social activities, and initiatives promoting a healthy work-life balance. We foster a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone feels welcome, respected, and valued.
Arup is recognized as one of the best companies to work thanks to our flexibility policies. We also adhere to the Code of Principles of Generational Diversity, committing to equal opportunities regardless of age.
At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective where individuality is encouraged. Our strength comes from how we respect, share, and connect our diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas. You’ll have the opportunity to do socially useful work that has meaning - to Arup, to your career, and to the clients and communities we serve.

In close partnership with hardware and architecture teams, they enable new capabilities and deliver production‑grade tools used by leading semiconductor and systems companies.
Responsibilities
Develop and enhance compiler components for Tensilica/Xtensa architectures
Work on code generation, instruction selection, and core optimizations
Collaborate with hardware and architecture teams to enable new features
Analyze performance and debug compiler/system-level issues
Requirements
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
Approximately 2+ years of academic or industry experience in systems software, compilers, or low‑level development (flag for human review if strictly required)
Strong programming skills in C and/or C++
Foundational understanding of compiler concepts and/or computer architecture
Nice To Have
Exposure to LLVM, GCC, or similar compiler frameworks
Experience with embedded systems or performance analysis
Familiarity with assembly language

jobs.title: Localization Engineer (With language Skills)
jobs.desc:
Role Summary
We are seeking an innovative and technically minded Globalization Engineer (Language Specialist) to join our Globalization Engineering team.
This role combines deep linguistic expertise with technology, automation, AI innovation, and process optimization to help deliver exceptional multilingual customer experiences across global markets. The successful candidate will play a critical role in driving AI adoption, redesigning localization workflows & Quality Processes, automating manual processes, managing linguistic assets, and ensuring the highest standards of language quality across products, content, and customer-facing experiences.
This position is ideal for an individual who is passionate about languages, technology, artificial intelligence, and operational excellence, and who wants to help shape the future of AI-enabled localization and globalization.
This is a Hybrid position located in Ireland. You may be required to be onsite on an as-needed basis. We are only considering candidates in Ireland and are not offering relocation assistance at this time.
Position Details
About The Role
AI, Automation & Innovation
Drive the adoption of AI-powered localization technologies and workflows.
Identify opportunities to leverage Generative AI, Machine Translation, Large Language Models (LLMs), and automation technologies to improve scalability, quality, and efficiency.
Evaluate emerging AI solutions and recommend innovative approaches to improve multilingual customer experiences.
Design and implement process improvements that reduce manual effort and accelerate delivery.
Develop and support automation solutions using scripting, integrations, and workflow technologies.
Contribute to the evolution of AI-enabled globalization and localization engineering practices.
Language Quality & Linguistic Excellence
Serve as a linguistic subject matter expert for one or more European languages.
Conduct linguistic quality assurance (LQA) activities and drive continuous quality improvement initiatives.
Define and maintain language quality standards, style guides, terminology, and best practices.
Ensure multilingual content is linguistically accurate, culturally appropriate, and aligned with brand standards.
Partner with stakeholders to resolve linguistic challenges and improve localization outcomes.
Linguistic Assets & AI Language Resources
Own and manage critical linguistic assets used across localization and AI initiatives.
Curate, develop, maintain, and govern:
Terminology databases
Translation memories
Taxonomies
Ontologies
Style guides
Language standards
AI evaluation datasets
Establish governance processes that ensure consistency, quality, reusability, and scalability of language resources.
Support the development of multilingual language assets that improve AI performance and customer experiences.
About You
Required Skills
Native or near-native proficiency in at least one of these languages - Italian / German / French / Dutch/ Brazilian / Portuguese.
Strong linguistic expertise and understanding of localization best practices.
Experience working in localization engineering, Localization QA, language technology, globalization, content operations, or a related field.
Experience with Localization Management Systems (TMS) and localization technologies.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Demonstrated experience improving workflows and operational processes.
Experience in / exposure to Software Development / Automation and in introductory level. (Python, CSharp Preferable)
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to work effectively in a global and highly collaborative environment.
Passion for technology, innovation, AI, language quality, and customer experience.
Preferred Skills
AI & Emerging Technology
Experience using Generative AI platforms such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or similar technologies.
Prompt engineering experience.
Experience evaluating AI-generated multilingual content.
Knowledge of AI governance, AI quality evaluation, and Responsible AI principles.
Familiarity with AI agents, autonomous workflows, and agent orchestration concepts.
Understanding of AI knowledge systems.
Automation & Technical Skills
Python scripting and automation experience.
Experience working with REST APIs and system integrations.

Amazon Leo is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon Leo will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.
At Amazon Leo, our Technical Customer Support Associates (TCSA) deliver timely, accurate, and professional general and technical support to all Amazon Leo customers. The Amazon Leo Customer Support (CS) team is looking for driven individuals who are up to the challenge of solving customer issues while providing positive customer experience. TCSA are technically savvy problem-solvers with a focus on customer account security. An ideal candidate would be an excellent listener, handle change easily, be a quick learner and critical thinker, and be able to handle ambiguity. The position requires the ability to communicate professionally, with maturity and self-confidence, in German/French and English.
Shifts are assigned on a rotational basis and may include early mornings, evenings, overnights, weekends and public holidays. You will be required to work all shift patterns.

Receive and manage customer escalations from Tier 1 support, delivering timely and effective resolutions across phone, email, and chat channels.
Offer detailed technical support with clear and professional communication
Collaborate with other customer support teams to resolve complex issues
Document steps and resolutions in a clear, easy-to-follow format
Identify trends in customer issues and propose improvements to support processes
Help create knowledge base articles and team documentation
Stay current on new Amazon Leo products and features
A day in the life
As a Tier 2 Technical Support Associate, you'll be at the heart of our global connectivity mission. Your day will be dynamic, and purpose driven. You'll engage with customers, troubleshoot intricate technical issues, and collaborate with leadership and cross-functional teams to ensure seamless service delivery. Each interaction is an opportunity to make a tangible difference in someone's ability to connect, learn, and grow.

Amazon Leo Global Operations is part of the Worldwide Consumer team. Experience using strong customer service, communication, and interpersonal skills
Experience communicating technical details verbally and in writing
Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays

Strong problem-solving skills with a drive to dig into the details of systems and processes to resolve customer issues
Excellent communication skills and ability to convey insights from complex analyses to internal and end customers
